words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.ex: He paid 1000 yen for the sushi.
words.ex_cn: 他用一千日元买了寿司。
words.en: The yen is the unit of currency used in Japan. It can also mean a strong desire or craving for something.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.tr:
adv. 小心地；谨慎地
adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He walked gingerly on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心翼翼地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you do something gingerly, you do it in a careful manner, usually because you expect it to be dangerous, unpleasant, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.ex: The buxom woman smiled warmly at the children.
words.ex_cn: 这位丰满的女士对孩子们温暖地笑了。
words.en: If you describe a woman as buxom, you mean that she has a full, rounded figure and is usually large-breasted.

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.tr:
adj. 柔和的；减弱的；郁郁不乐的
v. 征服；克制；制服；“subdue”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The room had subdued lights.
words.ex_cn: 房间里灯光柔和。
words.en: If a color or light is subdued, it is not very bright.

words.tr:
adj. 行乞的
n. 乞丐
words.ex: The mendicant monks wandered the streets, seeking alms.
words.ex_cn: 托钵僧在街上徘徊，寻求施舍。
words.en: A mendicant is someone who lives by asking people for money or food, especially as a member of a religious group that does this as a way of life.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.tr: n. 光环；光轮；日晕；月晕
words.ex: The sun had a golden aureole around it.
words.ex_cn: 太阳周围有一个金色的光晕。
words.en: An aureole is a circle of light or radiance surrounding the head or body of a sacred personage in art.

words.tr: v. 连续猛击；反复拳打；捶打
words.ex: The boxer pummels his opponent with fast punches.
words.ex_cn: 拳击手用快速的拳击击打他的对手。
words.en: To pummel someone or something means to hit them many times using your fists.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had fitful sleep last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚睡得断断续续。
words.en: Something that is fitful happens for irregular periods of time or occurs at irregular times, rather than being continuous.

words.ex: He took a hiatus from work to travel.
words.ex_cn: 他休假去旅行了。
words.en: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, series, or process.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: The priest used the catechism to teach the children about the faith.
words.ex_cn: 牧师使用教义问答书来教导孩子们关于信仰的知识。
words.en: A catechism is a summary of the principles of Christian religion in the form of questions and answers, used for the instruction of Christians.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.ex: He spoke in a reverent tone as he described the ancient temple.
words.ex_cn: 他在描述这座古老寺庙时，语气恭敬。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as reverent, you mean that they are showing great respect for a person or thing.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.tr: n. 心乱；失去冷静；不安
words.ex: The bad news caused her discomposure.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息让她心乱。
words.en: A state of being disturbed or agitated; uneasiness.

words.tr: n. 自明之理；不言而喻的道理；老生常谈
words.ex: It is a truism that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾，这是一个不言而喻的事实。
words.en: A truism is a statement that is obviously true and says nothing new or interesting.

words.tr: n. 年鉴；编年史；历史记载；年报
words.ex: The annals of history record many great kings.
words.ex_cn: 历史年鉴记录了许多伟大的国王。
words.en: A chronological record of events, especially those of a particular organization, institution, or community.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: He made an uncouth remark at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐时说了句粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe a person as uncouth, you mean that their behavior is vulgar, rude, or socially unacceptable.

words.tr:
adj. 不信宗教的；异教徒的；不信仰的
n. 异教徒
words.ex: He is an infidel who never goes to church.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不去教堂的不信宗教的人。
words.en: An infidel is a person who does not believe in a religion that someone regards as the true religion.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.tr: v. 沸腾；翻涌；骚动；激昂；大发雷霆
words.ex: The water began to seethe on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 水在炉子上开始沸腾。
words.en: If you say that someone is seething, you mean that they are very angry, but they are trying not to show it.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr:
adj. 倒退的；退化的；退步的
v. 逆行；倒退；堕落
words.ex: The company's retrograde policies led to a decline in productivity.
words.ex_cn: 公司倒退的政策导致了生产力的下降。
words.en: If you describe an action or idea as retrograde, you disapprove of it because it returns to old ideas or methods and does not take advantage of recent progress.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: n. 性受虐狂者；受虐狂者
words.ex: He revealed himself to be a masochist, enjoying the pain inflicted on him.
words.ex_cn: 他透露自己是一个受虐狂，喜欢别人施加在他身上的痛苦。
words.en: A masochist is someone who enjoys receiving pain or humiliation, especially in a sexual context.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.tr: adj. 无菌的；经消毒的；冷漠的
words.ex: The nurse used an aseptic technique to clean the wound.
words.ex_cn: 护士使用无菌技术清洁伤口。
words.en: Free from contamination caused by harmful bacteria, viruses, or other microorganisms; surgically clean or sterile.

words.tr:
n. 荨麻
v. 激怒
words.ex: The child touched the nettle and got a rash.
words.ex_cn: 孩子碰了荨麻，皮肤起了疹子。
words.en: A nettle is a wild plant with leaves that sting when you touch them. If you are nettled by something, it makes you annoyed or angry.

words.ex: He loves studying jurisprudence to understand laws better.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习法学以更好地理解法律。
words.en: Jurisprudence is the study of law and the principles on which law is based.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 难消化的，使人胀饱的；古板的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The stodgy pudding made him feel full and uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这道难消化的布丁让他感到胀满不适。
words.en: If you describe something as stodgy, you mean that it is dull, boring, and rather formal.

words.tr: adj. 拖拉的；拖沓的；磨蹭的
words.ex: He gave a dilatory answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题回答得很拖拉。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dilatory, you mean that they are slow and cause delay.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: His words showed great acerbity.
words.ex_cn: 他的话表现出极大的尖刻。
words.en: Acerbity refers to a sharp bitterness or severity of temper or expression.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The diaphanous curtain let in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄纱窗帘让晨光透了进来。
words.en: A diaphanous substance or fabric is very thin and almost transparent.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: The rocket has a propulsive engine.
words.ex_cn: 这枚火箭有一个推进引擎。
words.en: Relating to or capable of propelling or driving forward.

words.tr: adj. 无可指责的；无过失的
words.ex: Her behavior has always been irreproachable.
words.ex_cn: 她的行为一直无可指责。
words.en: If you say that someone's character or behaviour is irreproachable, you mean that they behave so well that they cannot be criticized.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.ex: She tried to browbeat him into submission.
words.ex_cn: 她试图恫吓他屈服。
words.en: To intimidate or bully someone into doing something, especially by using threats or aggressive behavior.

words.tr:
n. 表；名单；
v. 列出；
words.ex: He wrote his name on the list.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己的名字写在了表上。
words.en: A list is a set of items, especially names, written or printed one after the other.

words.ex: He reads fantasy books for escapism.
words.ex_cn: 他读奇幻小说来逃避现实。
words.en: Escapism is the tendency to seek distraction and relief from unpleasant realities, especially by seeking entertainment or engaging in fantasy.

words.tr: n. 小团体；小圈子；志同道合的一伙
words.ex: He belongs to a small coterie of artists.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个小艺术家圈子的成员。
words.en: A coterie is a small group of people with shared interests or tastes, especially one that is exclusive of other people.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: The memory of her smile is indelible.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的记忆是无法磨灭的。
words.en: If you say that something leaves an indelible impression, you mean that it is very unlikely to be forgotten.

words.ex: The medical students studied the anatomy of the cadaver.
words.ex_cn: 医学生们研究了尸体的解剖结构。
words.en: A dead body, especially one that is intended for dissection.

words.tr:
adj. 习惯的
v. 使习惯（于）；“inure”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is inured to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对嘈杂的声音已经习惯了。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr: n. 不服从；不顺从；反抗
words.ex: The sergeant punished the soldier for insubordination.
words.ex_cn: 中士因不服从而惩罚了士兵。
words.en: Insubordination is the act of deliberately not obeying someone in authority.

words.ex: The repeal of the old law took effect last month.
words.ex_cn: 这项旧法律的废止上个月生效了。
words.en: If the government repeals a law, it officially ends it, so that it is no longer valid.

words.ex: The virus made many people sick.
words.ex_cn: 这个病毒让很多人病了。
words.en: A virus is a very small organism that causes infectious diseases in people, animals, and plants.

words.tr: n. 泛滥；猛涨；大批；一连串
words.ex: A spate of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴雨淹没了街道。
words.en: A spate of things, especially unpleasant ones, is a large number of them that happen or appear within a short period of time.

words.ex: His comment was tangential to the main topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论离题了。
words.en: If you describe something as tangential, you mean that it has only a slight or indirect connection with the thing you are concerned with, and is therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.ex: The storm caused the train to halt.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使火车中断了。
words.en: Halting is used to describe something that is done in a hesitant or faltering manner, often because of uncertainty or lack of confidence.

words.tr:
v. 呆头呆脑地盯着
n. 呆子
words.ex: He just stood there gawking at the accident scene.
words.ex_cn: 他只是站在那里，呆呆地看着事故现场。
words.en: To gawk means to stare openly and stupidly.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.ex: The asteroid flew past Earth safely.
words.ex_cn: 这颗小行星安全地从地球旁飞过。
words.en: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun. Large numbers of these, ranging enormously in size, are found between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, though some have more eccentric orbits.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.tr: n. （礼炮）齐鸣；（火炮）齐射；一阵；一连串
words.ex: The ship fired a salvo to honor the visiting admiral.
words.ex_cn: 船只为致敬来访的海军上将鸣放了礼炮齐鸣。
words.en: A salvo is the simultaneous discharge of artillery or other guns in a battle, or a sudden outburst of applause or other noise.

words.tr: adj. 浮肿的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His legs looked turgid after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间走路后，双腿看起来浮肿了。
words.en: If you describe something such as a piece of writing or a speech as turgid, you think it is boring and difficult to understand because it is too serious or complicated.

words.ex: The dark clouds bode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something bodes ill, it makes you think that something bad will happen in the future. If something bodes well, it makes you think that something good will happen.

words.tr: adj. 甜蜜的；糖蜜似的；虚情假意的；过分多情的
words.ex: The song had a treacly melody that felt too sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌的旋律过于甜腻。
words.en: If you describe something as treacly, you dislike it because it is too sentimental or emotional.

words.ex: He inter his dog in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的狗关在后院里。
words.en: To place a dead body in the ground or in a tomb.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.ex: There is a correlation between exercise and good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼与健康之间存在相关性。
words.en: A correlation between things is a connection or link between them.

words.tr: adj. 有报酬的；有利益的；
words.ex: He took a remunerative job to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他找了一份有报酬的工作来养家。
words.en: providing payment; profitable

words.ex: The statute says drivers must stop at red lights.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律规定司机必须在红灯时停车。
words.en: A statute is a formal written law of a country or state, enacted by its legislative authority.

words.tr: n. 人物角色；假面；人格面具；
words.ex: The actor played a new persona in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中扮演了一个新的角色。
words.en: The aspect of someone's character that is presented to or perceived by others.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.tr: v. 使无效；抵消；废除；取消
words.ex: The judge will nullify the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法官将宣布该合同无效。
words.en: To nullify something means to make it have no effect or value.

words.ex: He took a remedial math course to improve his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一门补救数学课程来提高自己的技能。
words.en: Remedial actions or activities are intended to correct something that is wrong or to improve a bad situation.

words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.tr: adj. 每年落叶的；定期脱落的；非永久性的
words.ex: The trees lose their leaves in autumn because they are deciduous.
words.ex_cn: 这些树在秋天落叶，因为它们是落叶的。
words.en: Deciduous trees or plants lose their leaves in autumn or the dry season.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.ex: The rotundity of the marble ball made it roll smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 大理石球的球状使它滚动得很顺畅。
words.en: The quality or state of being round in shape.

words.tr:
adj. 不可挽救的；屡教不改的；不可救药的
n. 无可救药的人
words.ex: He is an incorrigible liar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个无可救药的骗子。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorrigible, you mean that they have faults which they seem unable or unwilling to correct, even though they are aware of them.

words.ex: People often stigmatize those with mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常污名化患有精神疾病的人。
words.en: If someone or something is stigmatized, they are unfairly regarded by many people as being bad or having something to be ashamed of.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: Ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人在纸莎草纸上写字。
words.en: Papyrus is a material similar to thick paper that was used in ancient times as a writing surface. It was made from the pith of the papyrus plant, Cyperus papyrus, a wetland sedge.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: n. 克拉（宝石重量单位）；开（含纯金的量）
words.ex: The diamond weighs two carats.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石重两克拉。
words.en: A unit of weight for precious stones and pearls, equivalent to 200 milligrams.

words.tr: adj. 温和宜人的（气候）；芳香的
words.ex: The balmy wind felt nice on her skin.
words.ex_cn: 温暖的微风轻拂她的皮肤。
words.en: Balmy weather is pleasantly warm and mild.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.tr:
n. 蜡；
v. 给…上蜡；
words.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造蜂巢。
words.en: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil that is used to make candles, polish, and other products. It can also refer to the process of applying wax to something or the natural substance found in the ear.

words.ex: The old book talked about necromancy and dead spirits.
words.ex_cn: 那本旧书讲的是巫术和亡灵。
words.en: Necromancy is the practice of magic involving communication with the dead – either by summoning their spirits as apparitions, visions or raising them bodily – for the purpose of divination, imparting the means to foretell future events or discover hidden knowledge, to bring someone back from the dead, or to use the dead as a weapon.

words.tr: n. 长诗的篇章（相当于书的一章）
words.ex: The poem is divided into several cantos.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗被分为几个篇章。
words.en: A canto is a principal division of a long poem or a section of a song.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: The ship docked at the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbor is a place on the coast where ships may moor in shelter, especially one protected from rough water by piers, jetties, and other artificial structures.

words.ex: The band will disband next month.
words.ex_cn: 这个乐队下个月将解散。
words.en: If someone disbands a group of people, or if the group disbands, it stops operating as a single unit.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: This information is relevant to our project.
words.ex_cn: 这些信息与我们的项目相关。
words.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

words.ex: The satellite sends pictures from space.
words.ex_cn: 卫星从太空发送图片。
words.en: A satellite is an object which has been sent into space in order to collect information or to be part of a communications system. Satellites move continually round the earth or around another planet.

words.ex: The priest's invocation helped the crowd feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 牧师的祈祷让人群感到平静。
words.en: An invocation is a request for help or forgiveness made to a god.

words.ex: She added ketchup as a condiment to her fries.
words.ex_cn: 她把番茄酱当作调味品加在薯条上。
words.en: A condiment is a substance such as salt, pepper, or mustard that you add to food when you eat it in order to improve the flavor.

words.ex: The bird's plumage was a vibrant mix of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟的羽毛色彩鲜艳。
words.en: The feathers covering the body of a bird.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.tr:
n. 别名；化名
adv. 又被称为；另外地
words.ex: He uses an alias to hide his real name.
words.ex_cn: 他使用一个化名来隐藏他的真实姓名。
words.en: An alias is a false or assumed identity, especially one used by a criminal.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.ex: He cooked the meal with gusto.
words.ex_cn: 他做这顿饭时很有兴趣。
words.en: If you do something with gusto, you do it with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The company must retrench to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司必须裁员以节省资金。
words.en: If a person or organization retrenches, they spend less money.

words.tr: adj. 性欲的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: The movie contains erotic scenes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含不适合儿童的色情场景。
words.en: Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement.

words.tr:
n. 松鸡；松鸡肉；怨言；牢骚
v. 抱怨；发牢骚
words.ex: The hunter saw a grouse in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎人在森林里看到一只松鸡。
words.en: A grouse is a bird with a plump body and feathered legs, belonging to the family Tetraonidae. As a verb, to grouse means to complain or grumble.

words.ex: The old rules have ossified over time.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧规则随着时间的推移变得僵化了。
words.en: To ossify means to change or develop into bone, or to become fixed and unable to change or develop.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.tr: adj. 狡猾的；诡计多端的
words.ex: The wily fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily, you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.ex: The wheelchair goes up the ramp easily.
words.ex_cn: 轮椅可以轻松地走上坡道。
words.en: A ramp is a sloping surface connecting two levels, such as a road or a path.

words.tr: adj. 应受谴责的；应受指责的；
words.ex: His lying to the teacher was reprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师撒谎是应受谴责的。
words.en: If you think that someone's behavior is reprehensible, you think that it is very bad or unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 牧歌；无伴奏合唱歌曲
words.ex: The choir sang a beautiful madrigal at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团在音乐会上演唱了一首优美的牧歌。
words.en: A madrigal is a type of secular vocal music composition, usually a part song, of the Renaissance and early Baroque eras. Traditionally, madrigals were unaccompanied; the number of voices varied from two to eight, and most frequently from three to six.

words.ex: His irreverence towards the sacred object was met with shock and disapproval.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣物品的不敬行为遭到了震惊和反对。
words.en: Irreverence is a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously.

words.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.
words.ex_cn: 出行的方式是骑自行车。
words.en: A mode is a particular way or style in which something is done or experienced.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The children played in a small grove behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房子后面的小树林里玩耍。
words.en: A grove is a small group of trees.

words.ex: He did not deign to answer her question.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑于回答她的问题。
words.en: If someone deigns to do something, they do it unwillingly and with a feeling of superiority.

words.tr: n. 混合物；聚集物；集团化
words.ex: The conglomeration of small shops made a big mall.
words.ex_cn: 小商店的聚集形成了一家大型商场。
words.en: A conglomeration is a mixture of different things that are found all together.

words.tr: adj. 有进取心的；有魄力的；
words.ex: He is an enterprising boy who starts small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有进取心的男孩，会经营小生意。
words.en: If you describe someone as enterprising, you mean that they are willing to try out new, unusual ways of doing or achieving something.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.tr: v. 亲如兄弟；友善交往；和敌兵亲善
words.ex: They quickly began to fraternize with the locals.
words.ex_cn: 他们很快就开始与当地人友好交往。
words.en: If one group of people fraternize with another, they meet or spend time together in a friendly way, especially when they are not supposed to.

words.tr: adj. 勇敢的；无所畏惧的；不屈不挠的
words.ex: The dauntless firefighter ran into the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的消防员冲进了着火的建筑。
words.en: If you describe someone as dauntless, you mean they are not easily frightened or discouraged from doing something.

words.ex: He loves paleontology and finds dinosaur bones.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱古生物学，寻找恐龙骨头。
words.en: The branch of science concerned with fossil animals and plants.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.ex: The pied butterfly fluttered among the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 那只杂色蝴蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞。
words.en: Having patches of two or more colors, typically black and white.

words.ex: He carefully slid the sword into its scabbard.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地把剑插回鞘中。
words.en: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword, dagger, or other similar blade.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.ex: The rifle has a 5.56 mm caliber.
words.ex_cn: 这把步枪的口径是5.56毫米。
words.en: The caliber of something or someone is their quality, especially when this is high.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.tr: n. 档案材料；卷宗；病历
words.ex: The officer checked the dossier before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 官员在会议前检查了档案。
words.en: A dossier is a collection of papers containing detailed information about a particular person or subject.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the precipice, afraid to move.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边，不敢动。
words.en: A very steep or overhanging place on a cliff or mountain; a situation of great peril.

words.tr: n. 浮渣；废物；杂质；渣滓
words.ex: The factory removes dross from the melted metal.
words.ex_cn: 工厂从熔化的金属中去除杂质。
words.en: Waste or impure matter, especially that which is separated from metals during the process of smelting.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.ex: Her husband cooks dinner every night.
words.ex_cn: 她的丈夫每天晚上做晚饭。
words.en: A married man considered in relation to his spouse.

words.tr: n. 寡头政治；寡头统治集团；寡头统治的国家
words.ex: The country is ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群富有的商人寡头统治。
words.en: A form of government in which all power is vested in a few persons or in a dominant class or clique; government by the few.

words.ex: The car decelerate when it sees the red light.
words.ex_cn: 当汽车看到红灯时，它减速了。
words.en: If a vehicle or machine decelerates or if you decelerate it, it slows down.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.ex: The dog belongs to a phylum called chordata.
words.ex_cn: 狗属于一个叫做脊索动物门的门。
words.en: A major taxonomic group of organisms, ranking above a class and below a kingdom, and comprising organisms that share a common set of characteristics.

words.ex: They have a reciprocal agreement to help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们有一个互相帮助的互惠协议。
words.en: A reciprocal action or agreement involves two people or groups who do the same thing to each other or agree to help each other in a similar way.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.tr: n. 隐居处；修道院；偏僻的寺院
words.ex: The old monk lived in a small hermitage on the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位老僧人住在山上的一个小隐居处。
words.en: A hermitage is a place where a hermit lives in seclusion from the world.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.tr:
n. 发酵；酵素；动乱
v. （使）发酵；动乱
words.ex: The ferment of yeast makes bread rise.
words.ex_cn: 酵母的发酵使面包膨胀。
words.en: If a substance ferments or if it is fermented, it changes chemically because of the action of yeast or bacteria, often producing alcohol.

words.tr: n. 昏迷；不省人事；恍惚
words.ex: He fell into a stupor after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他陷入了昏迷状态。
words.en: A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.

words.ex: He was regarded as a clumsy lout by his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的同事们认为他是个笨拙的人。
words.en: A lout is a man who behaves in a rude and aggressive way.

words.ex: I can't swim.
words.ex_cn: 我不会游泳。
words.en: Cannot; used to indicate that something is not possible or allowed.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替者；冒名行骗者
words.ex: He was exposed as an impostor who had been posing as a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他被揭露为一个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: An impostor is someone who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive people.

words.tr: n. 违反语法；文法错误；举止失礼
words.ex: He made a solecism when he said 'between you and I'.
words.ex_cn: 当他说出'between you and I'时，犯了一个语法错误。
words.en: A solecism is a grammatical mistake in speech or writing, or a breach of etiquette.

words.ex: He cares only about money and things, showing strong materialism.
words.ex_cn: 他只关心金钱和物质，表现出强烈的实利主义。
words.en: Materialism is the belief that only physical matter exists, and that everything, including thought, feeling, mind, and will, can be explained in terms of matter and physical phenomena.

words.tr: n. 主张妇女参政的人
words.ex: She was a suffragist who fought for women's right to vote.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位为女性争取投票权而斗争的女权运动者。
words.en: A suffragist is someone who campaigns for the right to vote, especially for women.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The incandescent bulb gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 白炽灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: He lost his keys by a mischance.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心弄丢了钥匙。
words.en: An unlucky event or accident.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr: adj. 不受约束的；无拘无束的
words.ex: He sang uninhibited at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上毫无拘束地唱歌。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as uninhibited, you mean that they express their opinions and feelings openly, and behave as they want to, without worrying what other people think.

words.ex: The cafe attracts a young clientele.
words.ex_cn: 这家咖啡馆吸引了一群年轻的顾客。
words.en: The clientele of a business or organization are its customers or clients.

words.tr: n. 拖欠的款项；“arrear”的复数；
words.ex: He paid all his arrears last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周付清了所有拖欠的款项。
words.en: If someone is in arrears with their payments, or if their payments are in arrears, they have not paid the regular amounts of money that they should have paid.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.ex: He ate gruel for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了稀粥。
words.en: A thin liquid food of oatmeal or other meal boiled in milk or water.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.tr: adj. 劣质的；次品的；卑劣的
words.ex: He bought a shoddy chair that broke after one day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一把劣质的椅子，一天就坏了。
words.en: If you describe something as shoddy, you mean that it has been done or made carelessly or badly.

words.ex: He sat in the alcove and read a book.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在壁龛里看书。
words.en: An alcove is a small area in a room which is formed by one part of a wall being built further back than the rest of the wall.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.tr:
n. 嘎嘎叫声；庸医；冒充内行的人
v. 嘎嘎地叫；大声闲谈；冒充内行
words.ex: The duck made a loud quack.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子发出了响亮的嘎嘎叫声。
words.en: A quack is someone who pretends to have medical skills that they do not really possess. It can also refer to the sound a duck makes.

words.ex: The boy saw a pterodactyl in the dinosaur book.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在恐龙书中看到了翼手龙。
words.en: A pterodactyl is an extinct flying reptile of the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods, which had a long, pointed beak, a short tail, and a wingspan of up to 12 meters.

words.ex: A small rivulet flows through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 一条小溪流过森林。
words.en: A very small stream.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.ex: He supplicated for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求宽恕。
words.en: to ask for something in a humble way; to beg earnestly and humbly

words.ex: The ape climbed slowly up the tree.
words.ex_cn: 这只猿慢慢爬上了树。
words.en: An ape is a large primate that does not have a tail, for example a chimpanzee or gorilla.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.tr: n. 前锋；前卫；先头部队；先驱
words.ex: He is at the vanguard of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他在新技术的前沿。
words.en: The vanguard is the leading part of an advancing military formation. It has a broader meaning, signifying the forefront of any movement or field.

words.ex: He predetermines the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就决定了结果。
words.en: To decide or settle (something) in advance.

words.ex: The forest is home to a rich fauna.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是丰富动物群的家园。
words.en: The animals of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The king tried to subjugate the rebels.
words.ex_cn: 国王试图征服叛乱者。
words.en: To subjugate a country or group of people means to take complete control of them, especially by defeating them in a war.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.tr: n. 透视画；西洋景；立体模型
words.ex: The museum featured a diorama of prehistoric life.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆展示了一个史前生活的立体模型。
words.en: A diorama is a model representing a scene with three-dimensional figures, either in miniature or as a large-scale museum exhibit.

words.tr: n. 诘问者；激烈质问者
words.ex: The heckler shouted during the speech.
words.ex_cn: 那个挑衅者在演讲期间大喊大叫。
words.en: A heckler is someone who interrupts a performer or speaker, often with rude or aggressive comments.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.tr: v. 计算；“calculate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 计算的；
words.ex: He calculated the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算了总费用。
words.en: If something is calculated to have a particular effect, it is deliberately done in order to have that effect.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: A small fissure appeared in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上出现了一道小裂缝。
words.en: A fissure is a long, narrow opening or line of breakage made by cracking or splitting, especially in rock or earth.

words.tr: n. 小装饰品；廉价首饰
words.ex: She bought a small trinket at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一个小饰物。
words.en: A trinket is a small ornament or item of jewelry that is of little value.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.tr: n. 秘密行动；偷偷摸摸
words.ex: The cat moved in stealth to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫悄悄地移动去抓老鼠。
words.en: Stealth is the action of moving or behaving in a secretive way in order to avoid being noticed.

words.ex: The moon reached its apogee last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚月亮到达了远地点。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.ex: The word 'home' has a warm connotation.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词有温暖的含义。
words.en: An idea or feeling that a word invokes in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: He went berserk when he saw the mess in his room.
words.ex_cn: 他看到房间里的混乱时，气得发疯。
words.en: If someone goes berserk, they lose control of themselves and become very angry or violent.

words.ex: The matrix gave birth to all living things.
words.ex_cn: 母体孕育了所有生命。
words.en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；漂泊者；乞丐
adj. 流浪的；漂泊的
words.ex: The vagrant slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: A vagrant is someone who moves from place to place and does not have a permanent home or job.

words.ex: He paraphrased the poem in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的语言意译了这首诗。
words.en: To paraphrase means to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words, especially to achieve greater clarity.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.tr: n. 护身符；驱邪物；能产生奇迹的东西；法宝
words.ex: He wears a talisman for good luck.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一个护身符以求好运。
words.en: A talisman is an object which is believed to have magic powers to protect its owner or to bring good luck.

words.tr: adj. 淫秽的；败坏风俗的
words.ex: The play contains some bawdy jokes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这出戏包含一些不适合儿童的猥亵笑话。
words.en: Bawdy humor or language refers to jokes or remarks about sex in a way that some people find offensive.

words.ex: He has good spatial skills for drawing maps.
words.ex_cn: 他画地图有很好的空间能力。
words.en: Relating to or occupying space.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.tr: adj. 醋的；醋酸的；乙酸的
words.ex: The smell of acetic acid was overpowering.
words.ex_cn: 乙酸的气味非常刺鼻。
words.en: Relating to or containing acetic acid or vinegar.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；生硬的；粗哑的
words.ex: The old man gave a gruff answer.
words.ex_cn: 老人粗声粗气地回答了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as gruff, you mean that they seem rather unfriendly or bad-tempered.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.ex: They believed there was a conspiracy to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他们相信有人密谋隐瞒真相。
words.en: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group of people to do something harmful or illegal.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.ex: The doctor did an autopsy to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了尸检以查明死因。
words.en: An autopsy is a medical examination of a dead body to discover the cause of death.

words.tr: v. 废除；取消；宣告无效
words.ex: The court will annul the marriage.
words.ex_cn: 法院将宣布婚姻无效。
words.en: To annul something means to declare it invalid or to officially say that it no longer exists.

words.ex: He dreams of a perfect utopia where everyone is happy.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想一个每个人都很幸福的完美乌托邦。
words.en: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr:
v. 为 ... 上脚镣；束缚；限制
n. 脚镣；桎梏；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner was fettered with chains.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯被锁链束缚着。
words.en: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the feet, or something that confines or restrains.

words.ex: She bought a new coiffure for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一个新发型。
words.en: A coiffure is a hairstyle, especially an elaborate one.

words.ex: She wore a silver brooch on her coat.
words.ex_cn: 她把一枚银色胸针别在外套上。
words.en: A brooch is a piece of jewelry that has a pin at the back so it can be fastened to a dress, blouse, or coat.

words.ex: The company showed compliance with safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 该公司遵守了安全规定。
words.en: The act of complying with a wish, request, or demand; obedience.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: My forebear came from Ireland long ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先很久以前来自爱尔兰。
words.en: Your forebears are your ancestors, especially your grandparents or earlier relatives.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.tr:
n. 壁画
v. 作壁画
words.ex: The artist painted a fresco on the church wall.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家在教堂的墙上画了一幅湿壁画。
words.en: A fresco is a picture that is painted on a plastered wall when the plaster is still wet.

words.ex: The small town has a maritime history.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有着海洋历史。
words.en: Relating to the sea, especially in relation to seaborne trade or naval matters.

words.ex: He is a lexicographer who writes dictionaries.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位编写词典的词典编纂者。
words.en: A lexicographer is a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries.

words.ex: A little gnome lives in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 一个小精灵住在花园里。
words.en: A gnome is a legendary creature that is often depicted as a small, human-like figure that lives underground and guards treasure.

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.tr:
adj. 类人猿的；像猴的
n. 类人猿；猴
words.ex: The simian climbed quickly up the tree.
words.ex_cn: 那只猿猴迅速爬上了树。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or being a monkey or ape.

words.ex: He signed the paper under duress.
words.ex_cn: 他在胁迫下签了那张纸。
words.en: Duress is a situation in which someone is forced to do something against their will, typically by the use of threats or force.

words.tr: n. 否认；自我克制；放弃
words.ex: His abnegation of the truth made everyone sad.
words.ex_cn: 他对真相的否认让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: The act of renouncing or rejecting something, often used in the context of self-denial or the refusal of certain rights or privileges.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 会议的结果是一个新计划。
words.en: The final result or outcome of a situation or event.

words.ex: He is a multifaceted person who can sing, paint, and code.
words.ex_cn: 他是个多方面的人，会唱歌、绘画和编程。
words.en: Having many facets or aspects.

words.tr: n. 被社会遗弃者；贱民；底层民众
words.ex: He felt like a pariah in the community after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 丑闻之后，他在社区里感觉像个贱民。
words.en: A pariah is someone who is not accepted by a particular group, especially because they are believed to have done something wrong or unacceptable.

words.ex: The villain tried to decapitate the hero with a sword.
words.ex_cn: 反派试图用剑砍下英雄的头。
words.en: To decapitate someone means to cut off their head.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: The old man has a cataract in his right eye.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人右眼有白内障。
words.en: A cataract is a medical condition in which the lens of the eye becomes progressively opaque, resulting in blurred vision. It can also refer to a large waterfall.

words.tr:
n. 露营；野营
v. 野营；临时露营
words.ex: The soldiers set up a bivouac for the night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们为过夜搭建了露营地。
words.en: A bivouac is a temporary camp or shelter, often used by soldiers or mountaineers, that does not use tents or other structures.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.tr:
adj. 教条（主义）的；空谈理论的
n. 教条主义者；空论家
words.ex: He is a doctrinaire who always follows rules strictly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个教条主义者，总是严格遵守规则。
words.en: If you say that someone is doctrinaire, you are criticizing them for following fixed theories or principles rather than considering practical problems.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr:
v. 拙劣地做；搞砸
n. 搞糟了的事情；失误
words.ex: He bungled the simple task.
words.ex_cn: 他把简单的任务搞砸了。
words.en: To bungle something means to do it badly or clumsily, often resulting in failure or mistakes.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr: n. 骑兵队、车队等的行列
words.ex: A cavalcade of horses passed through the town.
words.ex_cn: 一队马匹经过了这个小镇。
words.en: A cavalcade is a procession of people on horses or in vehicles, especially one that is part of a ceremony or celebration.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.tr:
adj. 有斑点的；斑驳的
v. （使）有斑纹；“dapple”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The dappled sunlight fell on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 斑驳的阳光洒在草地上。
words.en: Something that is dappled is marked with spots of a different color or shade.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.tr: n. 自动装置；机器人；机器人似的人
words.ex: The factory was filled with automatons that performed repetitive tasks.
words.ex_cn: 工厂里满是执行重复任务的自动机。
words.en: An automaton is a machine that operates on its own without the need for human control, especially a robot in the form of a human.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.ex: His craftiness helped him win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的狡猾帮助他赢得了比赛。
words.en: Craftiness is the quality of being clever at planning something so that you get what you want, especially by deceiving other people.

words.ex: The children played on a small knoll near the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园附近的一个小土丘上玩耍。
words.en: A small hill or mound.

words.tr:
v. 同意；赞成
n. 同意；赞成
words.ex: He gave his assent to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了这个计划。
words.en: If you assent to something, you agree to it or agree with it.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: He made an extrapolation from the data to predict the future.
words.ex_cn: 他根据数据做出了外推以预测未来。
words.en: Extrapolation is the act of estimating or concluding something by assuming that existing trends will continue or a current method will remain applicable.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.ex: The soldier did reconnaissance before the mission.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在任务前进行了侦察。
words.en: Reconnaissance is the military activity of obtaining information about an enemy's position, strength, or intentions by sending out small groups of soldiers or by using aircraft.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.tr: n. 丰饶的山羊角；聚宝盆；丰饶角
words.ex: The Thanksgiving table had a cornucopia of fruits and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 感恩节的餐桌上摆满了水果和蔬菜的丰饶山羊角。
words.en: A cornucopia is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly represented as a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts.

words.ex: He visited a podiatrist for his sore feet.
words.ex_cn: 他因为脚疼去看足病医生。
words.en: A podiatrist is a medical professional devoted to the study and medical treatment of disorders of the foot, ankle, and lower extremity.

words.tr: n. （年纪大的）坏脾气的人；脾气暴躁的人
words.ex: He was known as a curmudgeon who rarely smiled.
words.ex_cn: 他以脾气坏著称，很少笑。
words.en: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered or difficult person, especially an old one.

words.tr:
n. 谷壳；糠；揶揄
v. 开玩笑；戏弄
words.ex: The wind blew away the chaff from the wheat.
words.ex_cn: 风吹走了小麦中的糠秕。
words.en: Chaff is the outer covering of the seeds of grain such as wheat, which is separated from the grain before it is used as food.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: She daubed the wall with paint.
words.ex_cn: 她在墙上随意涂抹颜料。
words.en: To daub means to spread a substance such as paint, mud, or oil over a surface in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.tr: n. 堕落；道德败坏；腐化
words.ex: The depravity of his crimes shocked the community.
words.ex_cn: 他罪行的堕落程度震惊了整个社区。
words.en: Depravity is the state of being morally bad or evil.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.tr:
n. 日食；月食；黯然失色
v. 使失色
words.ex: We watched the solar eclipse last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚观看了日食。
words.en: An eclipse occurs when one celestial body moves into the shadow of another, temporarily obscuring it or cutting off its light.

words.ex: Can you tell me the gist of the story?
words.ex_cn: 你能告诉我这个故事的要点吗？
words.en: The main or essential part of a matter.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；法定的；义务的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is mandatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制的。
words.en: If something is mandatory, it is required by law or by a rule or regulation.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.ex: The general used a clever stratagem to win the battle.
words.ex_cn: 将军使用了一个巧妙的战略赢得了战斗。
words.en: A stratagem is a plan or scheme, especially one used to outwit an opponent or achieve an end.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.tr: adj. 多籽的；褴褛的；邋遢的；脏乱的
words.ex: The watermelon has a seedy center.
words.ex_cn: 西瓜的中心有很多籽。
words.en: If you describe a place or person as seedy, you disapprove of them because they look dirty and untidy, or they have a bad reputation.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.tr: adj. 不真诚的；不坦率的；虚伪的
words.ex: He gave a disingenuous answer to avoid trouble.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不真诚的回答以避免麻烦。
words.en: Someone who is disingenuous is not sincere or honest, but pretends to be so in order to deceive people.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.tr: n. 蓄意破坏者；破坏分子
words.ex: The saboteur tried to disrupt the operation by cutting the power lines.
words.ex_cn: 破坏者试图通过切断电源线来破坏运营。
words.en: A saboteur is a person who deliberately destroys or damages something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.ex: He wore the hat with panache.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着那顶帽子，显得很夸耀。
words.en: If you do something with panache, you do it in a confident, stylish, and elegant way.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.ex: The fish has a sharp barb on its tail.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的尾巴上有一个尖锐的倒刺。
words.en: A barb is a sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, which is angled away from the main point so as to make extraction difficult. It can also refer to a remark that is meant to hurt someone's feelings.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: His sojourn in Paris lasted two years.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎旅居了两年。
words.en: A sojourn is a temporary stay in a place.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.tr: adj. 垂头丧气的；灰心失望的
words.ex: He looked crestfallen after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后看起来垂头丧气。
words.en: If you are crestfallen, you are disappointed and sad because of something that has happened.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.tr: v. 使沮丧气馁；使灰心
words.ex: The bad news disheartened the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队灰心了。
words.en: To dishearten someone means to cause them to lose hope or enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 记忆的；记忆术的；增进记忆的
words.ex: He used a mnemonic rhyme to remember the dates.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一首记忆性的押韵诗来记住这些日期。
words.en: A mnemonic is something such as a very short poem or a special word used to help a person remember something, especially in the context of learning.

words.tr: v. 脱去…的法衣；免去…的圣职
words.ex: The priest was unfrocked for his misconduct.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧师因行为不端而被解除僧职。
words.en: To remove someone from their position as a priest or minister, especially as a punishment.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；苦涩的；刺激的；尖刻的
words.ex: The smoke from the fire had an acrid smell.
words.ex_cn: 火灾的烟雾有一种刺鼻的气味。
words.en: An acrid smell or taste is strong and sharp, and usually unpleasant. It can also describe a manner or expression that is bitter or harsh.

words.ex: The law is retroactive and covers last year.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律具有追溯效力，适用于去年。
words.en: If a decision, action, or law is retroactive, it is intended to take effect from a date before it was actually made.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 符合的；一致的；全等的
words.ex: The two shapes are congruent in size.
words.ex_cn: 这两个形状大小相符。
words.en: If one thing is congruent with another, they are similar or fit together well.

words.ex: The teacher made an emendation to the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师对文本做了一处修改。
words.en: the act of making corrections or improvements to a text

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.
