words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.tr:
adj. 已故的；不复存在的
n. 死者
words.ex: The defunct company no longer exists.
words.ex_cn: 这家已故的公司不再存在。
words.en: No longer existing or functioning; dead or inactive.

words.tr: adj. 颤抖的；战栗的；畏缩的
words.ex: Her voice was tremulous when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时声音颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice, smile, or actions are tremulous, they are unsteady because the person is uncertain, afraid, or upset.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.tr: adv. 斜视地；怀疑地；不赞许地
words.ex: He looked askance at the strange offer.
words.ex_cn: 他斜眼看着这个奇怪的提议。
words.en: If you look askance at something, you look at it in a way that shows you are suspicious or do not approve of it.

words.ex: The bard sang a song about love and war.
words.ex_cn: 这位吟游诗人唱了一首关于爱情与战争的歌。
words.en: A bard is a poet, traditionally one who recites epic poems and is associated with a particular oral tradition.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave him an anesthetic before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他用了麻醉剂。
words.en: An anesthetic is a substance that causes loss of sensation or consciousness, used especially to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.tr: n. 钟舌；铃舌；舌头；拍击之人或物；鼓掌的人
words.ex: The clapper hit the bell to make a loud sound.
words.ex_cn: 钟舌敲击钟体发出响亮的声音。
words.en: The part of a bell that strikes the bell to produce sound.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr: adj. 使用多种语言的；说多种语言的；
words.ex: He is a multilingual teacher who speaks three languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说三种语言的多语言教师。
words.en: Using or able to use several languages.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；自然的；不做作的
words.ex: Her artless smile made everyone feel at ease.
words.ex_cn: 她那天真的微笑让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If you describe someone as artless, you mean that they are simple and honest, and do not try to deceive other people.

words.ex: He learned the etymology of the word 'phone'.
words.ex_cn: 他学习了单词 'phone' 的词源。
words.en: Etymology is the study of the origin of words and the way in which their meanings have changed throughout history.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.tr: adj. 单色的； 单频的（光、辐射等）
words.ex: The painting is monochromatic, using only shades of blue.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是单色的，只使用了不同深浅的蓝色。
words.en: Consisting of one color or wavelength.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；生染的； v. “ingrain”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His ingrained habits are hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 他根深蒂固的习惯很难改变。
words.en: If something is ingrained, it is firmly established and therefore difficult to change.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.ex: The appellation 'Doctor' is used to address a person with a medical degree.
words.ex_cn: 称呼 'Doctor' 用于称呼拥有医学学位的人。
words.en: An appellation is a name or title that someone or something is known by.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 漂亮的；迷人的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The winsome girl smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个可爱的女孩对每个人微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as winsome, you mean that they are attractive and charming.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

words.tr: adj. 泥土的；粗俗的；朴实的
words.ex: The soil has an earthy smell after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，土壤有一种泥土的气味。
words.en: Something that is earthy is simple and not complicated, and often relates to the natural world or to basic human needs and experiences.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr: n. 低廉花哨的首饰；美观而无价值的东西
words.ex: She wore a necklace adorned with colorful baubles.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条饰有彩色小饰物的项链。
words.en: A bauble is a small, cheap ornament or piece of jewelry.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.ex: The government decided to codify the old laws.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定将旧法律编纂成典。
words.en: To codify means to arrange laws, rules, etc. into a systematic code.

words.tr: n. 蝰蛇；毒蛇；阴险恶毒的人
words.ex: The viper's venom is highly toxic.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒蛇的毒液有极高的毒性。
words.en: A viper is a type of snake that has long, hollow fangs through which it injects venom into its prey or enemies.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.tr:
adj. 滑稽的
n. 小丑；丑角
words.ex: The zany clown made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯狂的小丑让所有人都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as zany, you mean that they are strange or eccentric in a humorous way.

words.tr:
v. 挥；舞动；炫耀地显示
n. 挥舞
words.ex: He brandished a knife to scare the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他挥舞着一把刀吓唬小偷。
words.en: If you brandish something, especially a weapon, you wave it about in a threatening way.

words.ex: The children love watching animated movies.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢看动画电影。
words.en: Animated means full of life or excitement, or made to appear to move as if by magic or technology.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.ex: The violin played a plaintive melody.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴演奏了一首哀伤的旋律。
words.en: A plaintive sound or voice expresses sadness.

words.ex: She felt great felicity when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当她赢得奖品时，她感到极大的幸福。
words.en: Felicity is great happiness and pleasure.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.tr:
n. 供过于求；过量
v. 使充满；过量供应
words.ex: The market has a glut of cheap phones.
words.ex_cn: 市场上廉价手机泛滥。
words.en: An excessive supply of something, more than is needed, wanted, or can be used; to supply or fill to excess.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.tr: adj. 拟人的；赋予人性的；神人同形同性论的
words.ex: The cartoon characters were anthropomorphic animals.
words.ex_cn: 卡通角色是拟人化的动物。
words.en: Anthropomorphic refers to the attribution of human traits, emotions, or intentions to non-human entities.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.tr:
n. 诱饵；（诱捕鸟兽的）动物
v. 引诱
words.ex: The hunter used a decoy to attract ducks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用假鸭子来吸引鸭子。
words.en: A decoy is a person, thing, or action that is used to trick someone into doing something or going somewhere, especially by making them think they are going to get something they want.

words.tr: n. 皮肤病学家；皮肤科医生
words.ex: He visited a dermatologist for his skin rash.
words.ex_cn: 他因为皮肤疹去看皮肤科医生。
words.en: A dermatologist is a doctor who specializes in the study, diagnosis, and treatment of skin disorders and diseases.

words.tr: v. 专横；跋扈；盛气凌人
words.ex: He tries to domineer over his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图对弟弟发号施令。
words.en: To domineer means to rule over or control others in a harsh or arrogant way.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.tr: v. 教唆；收买；贿赂某人作伪证
words.ex: He tried to suborn a witness with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱收买证人。
words.en: To induce someone to commit an unlawful or wrongful act, especially to give false testimony in court.

words.tr: n. 围长；周长；肚带；腰围
words.ex: The tree has a large girth.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干很粗。
words.en: The distance around something, especially the middle part of a person's body or a tree.

words.tr: adj. 好管闲事的；爱干预的
words.ex: She was always meddlesome, poking her nose into everyone's business.
words.ex_cn: 她总是爱管闲事，把鼻子伸进每个人的事务中。
words.en: If you describe a person as meddlesome, you are criticizing them because they try to influence or change things that do not concern them.

words.tr:
v. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
n. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
words.ex: He keeps sniveling about his broken toy.
words.ex_cn: 他一直哭哭啼啼地说他的玩具坏了。
words.en: If someone snivels, they cry or sniff in a way that irritates you.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.tr: n. 铜绿锈；（金属表面的）绿锈；（旧木器等表面）年久而产生的光泽；（有点儿…的）样子
words.ex: The patina on the old bronze statue added to its charm.
words.ex_cn: 旧青铜雕像上的铜绿增添了它的魅力。
words.en: A patina is a thin layer that forms on the surface of something, especially metal, often as a result of age or exposure to the air, and that is usually green or brown.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: The deer is herbivorous.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹿是食草的。
words.en: Herbivorous animals are those that feed on plants.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: He studied theology at a prestigious seminary.
words.ex_cn: 他在一所著名的神学院学习神学。
words.en: A seminary is a college for training people to become priests or ministers.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.ex: He really loves his job.
words.ex_cn: 他真正地热爱他的工作。
words.en: You use really to emphasize that something is true or that it is the case.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The ruffian shouted at the old man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍对老人大喊大叫。
words.en: A ruffian is a violent, lawless person.

words.ex: People discuss politics on this forum.
words.ex_cn: 人们在这个论坛上讨论政治。
words.en: A forum is a place, situation, or group in which people exchange ideas and discuss issues, especially important public issues.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.ex: The rules show uniformity in all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则在所有学校中都保持一致。
words.en: The state or quality of being uniform; consistency.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅迎合素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater to someone or something means to provide them with all the things they need or want.

words.tr: adj. 单音节的；说话少而无礼的
words.ex: The word 'cat' is monosyllabic.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'cat' 是单音节的。
words.en: A monosyllabic word or utterance consists of only one syllable.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: He gave a synoptic view of the history.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史做了概括性的概述。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a synopsis; presenting a summary or general view of a whole.

words.ex: The seismic wave shook the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震波震动了地面。
words.en: Seismic means relating to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: The war caused terrible carnage on both sides.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争在双方都造成了惨烈的大屠杀。
words.en: The killing of a large number of people, especially in a violent way.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.tr: n. 好享受的人；贪图安逸的人
words.ex: He is a sybarite who loves luxury foods and soft beds.
words.ex_cn: 他是个享乐主义者，喜欢美味的食物和柔软的床。
words.en: A sybarite is someone who loves luxury and pleasure and tends to live a life of indulgence.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: The Philippines is an archipelago of thousands of islands.
words.ex_cn: 菲律宾是一个由数千个岛屿组成的群岛。
words.en: An archipelago is a group of islands, especially small islands, scattered in a body of water.

words.ex: He likes to dabble in various hobbies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢涉猎各种爱好。
words.en: If you dabble in something, you take part in it but not very seriously.

words.tr: n. 应得的惩罚；因果报应
words.ex: He lied too much, and now he got his comeuppance.
words.ex_cn: 他撒了太多谎，现在遭到报应了。
words.en: A punishment or retribution that someone deserves.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.ex: He rubbed the liniment on his sore muscles.
words.ex_cn: 他把药膏擦在酸痛的肌肉上。
words.en: A liniment is a liquid that you rub into the skin in order to reduce pain or stiffness.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: n. 突降；苍白无力的结尾；令人扫兴的结尾
words.ex: The movie ended with an anticlimax.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一个平淡的结局收尾。
words.en: An anticlimax is a disappointing end to an exciting or impressive series of events.

words.ex: She fought gamely despite her injuries.
words.ex_cn: 尽管受了伤，她还是勇敢地战斗。
words.en: In a brave and spirited manner; with pluck.

words.ex: The sleeper breathed deeply in the quiet room.
words.ex_cn: 睡眠者在安静的房间里深呼吸。
words.en: A sleeper is someone who is sleeping, or a thing that unexpectedly becomes very successful.

words.ex: The astral plane is believed to be a level of existence beyond the physical world.
words.ex_cn: 人们相信星界是超越物质世界的一个存在层面。
words.en: Relating to or resembling the stars.

words.tr:
n. 材料；原料；
adj. 物质的；
words.ex: The table is made of wood material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由木头材料制成的。
words.en: Material refers to the substance or substances from which a thing is made or can be made, or information or ideas for use in creating a book or other work.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr:
adj. 乱花钱的；挥霍的
n. 浪费金钱的人；挥金如土的人
words.ex: He is a spendthrift who buys things he doesn't need.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乱花钱的人，买很多不需要的东西。
words.en: A spendthrift is someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible way.

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: He showed his mettle in the tough race.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰苦的比赛中展现了实力。
words.en: Mettle is the ability and determination to do something successfully in spite of difficult conditions.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr: n. 发达的肌肉；膂力；腌制好的野猪肉
words.ex: He has brawn but not much brains.
words.ex_cn: 他力气大，但不太聪明。
words.en: Brawn refers to physical strength and muscularity, often in contrast to intelligence or brainpower.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: The suspect was arraigned in court yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 嫌疑人昨天在法庭上被传讯。
words.en: If someone is arraigned, they are brought to court and formally charged with a crime.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；翻找；乱翻
n. 翻箱倒柜的寻找
words.ex: He rummaged through his drawer to find the keys.
words.ex_cn: 他翻找抽屉找钥匙。
words.en: If you rummage through something, you search for something you want by moving things around in a careless or hurried way.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: The somnolent boy nodded off during class.
words.ex_cn: 那个昏昏欲睡的男孩在课堂上睡着了。
words.en: If you are somnolent, you feel sleepy.

words.ex: He denied the aspersion on his character.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对他人格的污蔑。
words.en: An aspersion is a remark or statement that criticizes someone or something and damages their reputation.

words.ex: The old eggs began to addle in the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧鸡蛋在热中开始腐臭。
words.en: If something addles someone's mind or brain, it confuses them and makes them unable to think clearly.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.tr:
n. 轭；枷锁；束缚
v. 上轭；使强行结合
words.ex: The farmer put a yoke on the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫给牛套上了轭。
words.en: A yoke is a wooden bar that is fastened over the necks of two animals, especially cattle, and connected to the vehicle or load that they are pulling. It can also refer to something that binds people together or something that people find oppressive.

words.tr: v. 供以服装；供以军用品；装备
words.ex: The soldiers were accoutered with the latest military gear.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们装备了最新的军用装备。
words.en: To equip or outfit someone with the necessary items or clothing for a particular purpose.

words.ex: His reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 他的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: To besmirch someone or something means to spoil their good reputation.

words.tr:
v. （使）磨损；（使）烦躁；（使）紧张
n. 磨损处；吵闹；争吵
words.ex: The rope began to fray after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子用了多年后开始磨损。
words.en: If something such as cloth or rope frays, or if something frays it, its threads or fibres start to come apart from each other and it becomes weaker. A situation of conflict or intense competition can also be referred to as a fray.

words.tr: n. 康塔塔；清唱剧；大合唱
words.ex: The choir sang a beautiful cantata last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 上个星期日，合唱团演唱了一首优美的清唱剧。
words.en: A cantata is a musical composition for voices and orchestra, typically in several movements, often involving a choir.

words.tr: n. 大笑；笑死我了 (used to express amusement)
words.ex: He told a funny joke and got a big lol.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个有趣的笑话，引得大家大笑。
words.en: To laugh out loud, especially in response to something humorous.

words.tr: adj. 溢于言表的；感情奔放的
words.ex: She was effusive in her praise for the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对老师的赞美非常热情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as effusive, you mean that they express pleasure, gratitude, or approval in a very enthusiastic way.

words.ex: He showed great continence by not eating the cake.
words.ex_cn: 他通过不吃蛋糕展现了极大的自制力。
words.en: The ability to control oneself, especially one's desires and impulses, particularly in the context of sexual activity.

words.tr: v. 租借；出租；“rend”的过去式和过去分词； n. 租金；
words.ex: They rent a small apartment in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们租了一间城市里的小公寓。
words.en: Rent refers to the payment made periodically by a tenant to a landlord for the use of property or land.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a placebo to see if his pain would go away.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一个安慰剂，看看他的疼痛是否会消失。
words.en: A substance that has no therapeutic effect, used as a control in testing new drugs, or given for its psychological effect to a patient who believes it to be a medicine.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.ex: His answer was too simplistic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太简单化了。
words.en: If you describe something as simplistic, you disapprove of it because it is so simple that it ignores important details or difficulties.

words.ex: He learned about his ancestry from his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖母那里了解了自己的血统。
words.en: Your ancestry is the series of ancestors from whom you are descended.

words.tr:
adj. 据说的；号称的；有名气的
v. 认为；以为；“repute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a reputed doctor in this city.
words.ex_cn: 他是这座城市里有名的医生。
words.en: Generally believed to be a particular thing, although this might not be true.

words.ex: The bombardment lasted for three hours.
words.ex_cn: 轰击持续了三个小时。
words.en: The act of attacking a place with bombs continuously and intensively.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.ex: He has aphasia after the stroke.
words.ex_cn: 他中风后得了失语症。
words.en: Aphasia is a condition that robs you of the ability to communicate. It can affect your ability to speak, write and understand language, both verbal and written.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.ex: He learned piano under his teacher's tutelage.
words.ex_cn: 他在老师的指导下学习钢琴。
words.en: The act of guarding, protecting, or guiding; the office or function of a guardian; guardianship; protection; as, the king's right of seigniory and tutelage.

words.ex: He cringed when he heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到巨大的噪音时，他畏缩了。
words.en: If you cringe at something, you feel embarrassed or disgusted, and perhaps show this feeling in your expression or by making a slight movement.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: He gave up worldly pleasures to live a simple life.
words.ex_cn: 他放弃了世俗的享乐，过着简朴的生活。
words.en: Worldly means relating to the world and the practical matters of life, rather than to spiritual or religious matters.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: The government will expropriate the land for the new road.
words.ex_cn: 政府将征用这块土地用于新建道路。
words.en: If a government or other authority expropriates someone's property, they take it away from them for public use or benefit.

words.tr:
n. 桌子；表格；台子；
v. 搁置；
words.ex: He put his books on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放在桌子上。
words.en: A table is a piece of furniture with a flat top that you put things on or use to do things such as eat, write, or work.

words.tr: n. 宣告无罪；无罪的判决
words.ex: The court gave him an acquittal after the trial.
words.ex_cn: 审判后，法院宣布他无罪。
words.en: An acquittal is a formal declaration in a court of law that someone who has been accused of a crime is not guilty.

words.ex: He decided to waive the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他决定放弃这笔费用。
words.en: If you waive a right, claim, or privilege, you do not insist on it or do not use it.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: He tried to wheedle money from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗父母给他钱。
words.en: If someone wheedles, they try to persuade someone to do or give them something, often by flattery or by being very nice.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: He absconded with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚携款逃跑了。
words.en: If someone absconds from somewhere, they leave there quickly and secretly because they have something to hide or are afraid of being caught.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.tr: n. 突然说出；射精；射出
words.ex: He shouted in anger, and his ejaculation surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他愤怒地喊叫，这句话突然说出，让所有人都吃了一惊。
words.en: The act of ejecting semen from the penis; a sudden exclamation or utterance.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The news roiled the financial markets.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息搅乱了金融市场。
words.en: To make (a liquid) turbid or muddy by stirring up sediment; to disturb or irritate.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.ex: He wore jeans to the informal party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着牛仔裤去参加非正式的聚会。
words.en: If you describe something as informal, you mean that it is not done or said in a formal or official way.

words.ex: The wedding party was held under a large marquee in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼派对在花园里的大帐篷下举行。
words.en: A marquee is a large tent used for social or commercial events, or the canopy over the entrance to a theater or cinema.

words.ex: He spoke with candor about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地谈到了自己的错误。
words.en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness.

words.tr: v. （使）留痕迹；做标记；评分；“mark”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 明显的；显著的；有记号的；
words.ex: The storm marked the old tree with deep scratches.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在那棵老树上留下了深深的划痕。
words.en: A marked change or difference is very obvious and easily noticed.

words.tr: adj. 狂乱的；狂暴的；疯狂似的； v. “frenzy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The crowd became frenzied when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群变得狂乱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenzied, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often wild.

words.tr: n. 自我陶醉者；自恋者
words.ex: He is a narcissist who only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只谈论自己的自恋者。
words.en: A narcissist is someone who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.

words.tr: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可战胜的
words.ex: The castle was impregnable during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争期间固若金汤。
words.en: An impregnable building or place is so strong and secure that it cannot be entered or captured by force.

words.ex: He loves entomology and collects bugs.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱昆虫学，喜欢收集昆虫。
words.en: The branch of zoology concerned with the study of insects.

words.ex: The choir sang a paean of praise for the retiring principal.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团为即将退休的校长唱了一首赞歌。
words.en: A paean is a song of praise, joy, or triumph.

words.ex: The king vouchsafed a generous grant to the university.
words.ex_cn: 国王慷慨地赐予了大学一笔赠款。
words.en: If you vouchsafe something to someone, you give or tell it to them, especially in a gracious or condescending manner.

words.ex: His comment was pure detraction.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论完全是诽谤。
words.en: Detraction refers to the act of taking away from the value or reputation of something or someone, often through criticism or slander.

words.ex: His impiety shocked the religious community.
words.ex_cn: 他的不敬震惊了宗教界。
words.en: Lack of piety or reverence, especially toward a god.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 无力的；虚弱的；阳痿的
words.ex: He felt impotent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到无能为力。
words.en: If someone feels impotent, they feel that they have no power to influence people or events.

words.ex: The soup was too bland for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太淡了，我不喜欢。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting.

words.ex: He was known as an apologist for the controversial theory.
words.ex_cn: 他以该争议理论的辩护者而闻名。
words.en: An apologist is someone who defends or justifies a particular idea, person, or institution, especially in a way that is considered to be too uncritical or forgiving.

words.tr:
adj. 离奇可笑的；滑稽古怪的
n. 小丑；滑稽演员
words.ex: His droll sense of humor always lightens the mood.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感总是能缓和气氛。
words.en: If you describe something as droll, you mean that it is amusing, especially in an odd or unusual way.

words.tr: n. 收割者；收获者；收割机
words.ex: The reaper cuts wheat in the field.
words.ex_cn: 收割者在田里收割小麦。
words.en: A reaper is a person or machine that cuts and gathers crops at harvest.

words.tr:
n. 协约；契约
v. 订立契约
words.ex: They made a covenant to always help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们立下契约，永远互相帮助。
words.en: A covenant is a formal agreement or promise between two or more people, often involving legal obligations.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.tr:
n. 小规模战斗；小争斗；小冲突
v. 进行一场小冲突
words.ex: The two boys had a small skirmish over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球发生了一场小冲突。
words.en: A skirmish is a minor battle or fight, often one that is part of a larger conflict.

words.ex: The passengers disembark at the port.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在港口上岸。
words.en: To disembark means to leave a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.

words.ex: The old man lives in a small hovel.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人住在一间小破屋里。
words.en: A hovel is a small, dirty, and often poorly built house or shelter.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.tr: adj. 流浪汉体裁小说的；以歹徒为题材的
words.ex: The novel tells a picaresque story of a poor boy traveling alone.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说讲述了一个穷男孩独自旅行的流浪汉式故事。
words.en: A picaresque story is one that involves a series of adventures or events in which the main character is usually a rogue or adventurer.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: He stepped on a shard of broken glass.
words.ex_cn: 他踩到了一块碎玻璃片。
words.en: A shard is a piece of broken glass, pottery, or metal.

words.ex: His geniality made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的和蔼可亲让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being friendly and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.tr: n. 指标；索引；指数；“index”的复数
words.ex: The company tracks key indices to measure performance.
words.ex_cn: 该公司追踪关键指标以衡量表现。
words.en: Indices are used to measure or indicate something, such as economic health or the performance of a stock market.

words.ex: His iconoclastic ideas changed the way people think about art.
words.ex_cn: 他打破旧习的想法改变了人们对艺术的看法。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as iconoclastic, you mean that they deliberately challenge established beliefs or institutions.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: The decomposition of the apple took weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果的分解花了几个星期。
words.en: Decomposition is the process by which organic substances are broken down into simpler organic or inorganic matter such as carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars and mineral salts.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: He kept his equanimity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴中保持了冷静。
words.en: If you face a difficult situation with equanimity, you remain calm and do not get upset or angry.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.tr:
n. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
v. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: If you countermand an order, you cancel it, usually by giving a different order.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: The sentinel stands guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 哨兵站在门口站岗。
words.en: A sentinel is a soldier or guard whose job is to stand and keep watch.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: The company preempted its rivals by launching the product early.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过提前推出产品抢先行动。
words.en: To preempt something means to do or say something before someone else does, especially to prevent them from doing or saying it.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr:
v. （艰难地）爬上；攀登
n. （艰难地）爬；攀登
words.ex: The boy clambered up the rocky hill.
words.ex_cn: 男孩爬上了多石的山丘。
words.en: If you clamber somewhere, you climb there with difficulty, usually using your hands as well as your feet.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.ex: The road inclines sharply to the top of the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这条路陡峭地倾斜向山顶。
words.en: If you incline to a particular opinion, you have a tendency to think or behave in a particular way.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.tr: n. 无家可归的人；流浪儿；无主的动物
words.ex: The waif was found wandering the streets alone.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪儿被发现独自一人在街上徘徊。
words.en: A waif is a person, especially a child, who has no home or friends and is very thin and poorly dressed.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.ex: The parallelism between the two events is striking.
words.ex_cn: 这两件事之间的相似之处非常明显。
words.en: Parallelism is the state of being parallel or of corresponding in some way.

words.ex: He has a rare malady that doctors are trying to cure.
words.ex_cn: 他患有一种罕见的疾病，医生们正在努力治疗。
words.en: A malady is a disease or illness.

words.ex: She abhors violence.
words.ex_cn: 她憎恶暴力。
words.en: If you abhor something, you hate it very much, especially because you think it is immoral or disgusting.

words.ex: The restaurant has a calm ambience.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一种宁静的氛围。
words.en: The character and atmosphere of a place.

words.ex: The lake offers quietude at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在日出时带来宁静。
words.en: A state of stillness, calmness, and quiet in a place or person.

words.ex: He escaped from servitude and found freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他逃离了奴役，获得了自由。
words.en: The state of being a slave or completely subject to someone more powerful.

words.tr: v. 浸入水中；泼上水；熄灭
words.ex: He doused the burning log in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把燃烧的木头浸入水中。
words.en: To douse something means to quickly throw water over it in order to put out a fire, or to pour a lot of liquid over it.

words.ex: The political situation in the country was like a maelstrom.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的政治局势就像一个大漩涡。
words.en: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool in the sea or a river, or a situation in which there is great confusion, violence, and destruction.

words.ex: The poem has four stanzas.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有四节。
words.en: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem that are separated from other groups by a space.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.ex: The teacher gave him an admonition for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他迟到而给了他一个警告。
words.en: An admonition is a warning or a piece of advice that is given to someone to correct their behavior or to prevent them from doing something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr: adj. 衰弱的；衰败的；软弱的
words.ex: The old king was effete and could not lead.
words.ex_cn: 这位老国王虚弱无能，无法领导。
words.en: No longer productive or effective; lacking the power or will to achieve or succeed.

words.ex: The newspaper published his obituary yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 报纸昨天刊登了他的讣告。
words.en: An obituary is a notice of a person's death, especially in a newspaper, often with a brief biography of the deceased.

words.tr:
n. 白鼬；雪貂
v. 用雪貂打猎；搜寻
words.ex: The ferret ran under the fence.
words.ex_cn: 白鼬从篱笆下跑过去了。
words.en: A ferret is a small, fierce animal which is used for hunting rabbits and rats. To ferret means to search for something persistently.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr:
n. 系绳；系链；界限
v. 用绳拴住
words.ex: The horse was tied to the post with a tether.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马被用拴绳系在了柱子上。
words.en: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal to a post or other fixed point so that it cannot move away.

words.tr: v. 潜伏；偷偷隐躲；鬼鬼祟祟地活动
words.ex: The cat skulked behind the bushes.
words.ex_cn: 猫躲在灌木丛后面鬼鬼祟祟地走。
words.en: If someone skulks somewhere, they move there in a quiet, secretive way, often because they are involved in something dishonest or because they do not want to be seen.

words.tr:
n. 救援；援助者
v. 救援
words.ex: The nurse gave succor to the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 护士向受伤的男人提供了援助。
words.en: Succor is assistance and support given to someone in times of hardship or distress.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.ex: The wind abrades the rock slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢磨损岩石。
words.en: To scrape or wear away by friction or erosion.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.tr:
v. 擦亮；磨光
n. 光泽
words.ex: He burnishes the old metal every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都抛光那块旧金属。
words.en: To burnish something means to polish it and make it shine by rubbing it.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The redoubtable warrior struck fear into the hearts of his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 那位令人敬畏的战士让敌人心生恐惧。
words.en: If you describe someone as redoubtable, you have great respect for their power and strength, and you may be afraid of them as well.

words.tr: n. 弹回；反响；后果；反射
words.ex: The ball showed a clear repercussion off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上明显地弹回。
words.en: The effect that an action, event, or decision has on something, especially a bad effect.

words.ex: The workers are climbing the scaffold to paint the building.
words.ex_cn: 工人们正在爬脚手架去粉刷大楼。
words.en: A scaffold is a temporary structure erected to support workers and materials during the construction, repair, or cleaning of a building or other large structure. It can also refer to a raised wooden platform used formerly for the public execution of criminals.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.tr: n. 大亨；巨头；大企业家；
words.ex: He became a tycoon after building a big oil company.
words.ex_cn: 他在建立了一家大型石油公司后成为了一位大亨。
words.en: A tycoon is a person who is successful in business or industry and has become rich and powerful.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.ex: The depredation of forests harms wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 森林的破坏危害了野生动物。
words.en: The act of preying upon or plundering; the act of laying waste; as, the depredations of an army on the country.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.tr: adj. 患狂犬病的；狂暴的；疯狂的
words.ex: The rabid dog ran wildly through the street.
words.ex_cn: 那只狂犬在街上狂奔。
words.en: If you describe someone as rabid, you mean that they have very strong and unreasonable opinions or beliefs about a subject, especially in politics.

words.tr:
n. 丛；笨重的脚步声；土块
v. 使成一丛；凝结成块；拖着沉重的步子走
words.ex: The grass formed a clump near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 草在篱笆附近长成了一簇。
words.en: A clump of things such as trees or plants is a small group of them growing together. A clump of earth or mud is a small, solid mass of it.

words.ex: The teacher changed the parameter to make the test easier.
words.ex_cn: 老师更改了参数，使测试更容易。
words.en: A parameter is a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity.

words.ex: The hiker stared into the dark abyss.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者凝视着黑暗的深渊。
words.en: An abyss is a very deep hole in the ground, or a very difficult or unpleasant situation that seems to have no end.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.tr:
v. 用布包裹；用绷带缠
n. 长而宽的一长条；割刈的带状地
words.ex: She swathed the baby in a soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 她用一条柔软的毯子把婴儿裹起来。
words.en: To wrap or bind in or as if in a bandage or cloth.

words.ex: They disinterred the body last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周把尸体挖了出来。
words.en: To dig up something that has been buried, especially a corpse.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.ex: The visa application requires a lot of formality.
words.ex_cn: 签证申请需要很多正式手续。
words.en: A formality is something that is done as part of a formal process or procedure, often without much thought or feeling because it is expected.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.tr: n. 纨绔子弟；花花公子
words.ex: He was considered a fop by his peers for his extravagant clothing choices.
words.ex_cn: 他的同龄人认为他是个花花公子，因为他过分讲究穿着。
words.en: A fop is a man who is very concerned about his clothes and appearance in a way that might seem silly or excessive.

words.ex: He is chary of spending money on useless things.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意把钱花在无用的东西上。
words.en: If you are chary of doing something, you are cautious or hesitant about doing it because you are worried that it might have bad consequences.

words.ex: The hue of the sky changed at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空的色调发生了变化。
words.en: A hue is a particular shade of a color.

words.ex: He led a dissolute life after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后过着放荡的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissolute, you mean they behave in a way that is considered immoral because they do things such as drink or have sex too much.

words.ex: He was known for his venturesome spirit and willingness to take risks.
words.ex_cn: 他以冒险精神和愿意承担风险而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as venturesome, you mean that they are willing to take risks, especially in order to try out new things.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.ex: The company made a titanic effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司做出了巨大的努力来按时完成项目。
words.en: If you describe something as titanic, you mean that it is very big or important, and usually that it involves very powerful forces.

words.tr: adj. 小束状的；稀疏的；纤弱的
words.ex: She has wispy hair that floats in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 她有轻盈的头发，在风中飘动。
words.en: Something that is wispy is thin and weak, and often seems to be floating or moving gently.

words.ex: The soldier was honored for his valor in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位士兵因在战斗中的英勇表现而受到表彰。
words.en: Valor is great courage, especially in a battle or war.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.ex: He ate a waffle with maple syrup for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一块淋上枫糖浆的华夫饼。
words.en: If you say that someone waffles, you are critical of them because they talk or write a lot without actually making any clear or important points.

words.ex: A fleck of paint fell on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 一小片油漆掉在了地上。
words.en: A fleck is a small mark or spot, especially one that is different in color or texture from the area around it.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: He believes in fatalism and does not try to change his fate.
words.ex_cn: 他相信宿命论，不愿改变自己的命运。
words.en: Fatalism is the belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.tr: n. 挥霍无度的人；败家子
words.ex: He was criticized for being a wastrel with his inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他因挥霍继承的财产而受到批评。
words.en: A wastrel is someone who wastes their time, money, or resources in a careless or irresponsible way.

words.tr: adj. 激起性欲的；满足感官的；撩人的
words.ex: The painting showed a voluptuous woman with flowing curves.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位身材性感、曲线优美的女人。
words.en: If you describe a woman as voluptuous, you mean that she has large breasts and hips and is considered sexually attractive.

words.ex: This book is about the realm of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于人工智能领域的。
words.en: A realm is a country ruled by a king or queen, or an area of activity, interest, or knowledge.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: The sea looks opalescent at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳下，大海呈现出虹彩光泽。
words.en: An opalescent object or color appears to change in different lights, showing soft, shimmering colors like those of an opal.

words.ex: The choir performed a beautiful requiem in memory of the deceased.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班为纪念逝者演唱了一首优美的安魂曲。
words.en: A requiem is a piece of music that is performed in a Catholic church in memory of someone who has died, or a piece of music that is similar to this and is performed in memory of someone who has died.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.ex: A quorum must be present to conduct official business.
words.ex_cn: 必须有法定人数在场才能进行正式业务。
words.en: A quorum is the minimum number of people that must be present at a meeting before it can officially begin and before official decisions can be taken.

words.ex: Every worker has an entitlement to fair pay.
words.ex_cn: 每位工人都有获得公平报酬的权利。
words.en: An entitlement is a right to have or do something, often granted by law or policy.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.tr: n. 荒野；[地理]沼泽；系泊（moor 的复数）; v. 使停泊；被系住（moor 的三单形式）
words.ex: The sheep walk on the moors near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在村庄附近的荒原上行走。
words.en: Moors are areas of open, uncultivated land, often covered with heather, that are found in parts of Britain and other countries.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不忠的；有叛意的
v. 使不满；使疏远；“disaffect”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The disaffected youth joined the protest.
words.ex_cn: 不满的青年加入了抗议活动。
words.en: If you are disaffected, you no longer support or are satisfied with something or someone, especially a group or organization that you used to support.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.tr: n. 编号作品；乐曲；艺术作品
words.ex: The composer's latest opus has received critical acclaim.
words.ex_cn: 这位作曲家的最新作品获得了评论界的好评。
words.en: An opus is a creative work, especially a musical composition or set of compositions numbered in order of publication.

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

words.ex: The pandemic caused many schools to close.
words.ex_cn: 这场流行病导致许多学校关闭。
words.en: A pandemic is an occurrence of a disease that affects many people over a wide area.

words.tr: adj. 膨胀的；肿胀的； v. “bloat”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The dog looked bloated after eating too much food.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗吃太多食物后看起来肚子膨胀。
words.en: If someone is bloated, they are swollen and round because they have eaten too much or are suffering from a medical condition.

words.ex: He gave a furtive look around before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前偷偷看了一眼四周。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive, you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.

words.ex: The fulcrum is the point on which a lever rests or is supported and on which it pivots.
words.ex_cn: 支点是杠杆所依靠或支撑的点，也是它旋转的中心。
words.en: A fulcrum is the support about which a lever turns, or something that plays a central role in or is in the center of a situation or activity.

words.ex: The anthropologist studies ancient tribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家研究古代部落。
words.en: An anthropologist is a person who studies anthropology, which is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.tr: adj. 宗派的；教派的；派别的；
words.ex: The conflict was fueled by sectarian tensions.
words.ex_cn: 这场冲突由宗派紧张局势加剧。
words.en: If you describe someone as sectarian, you mean that they belong to a particular sect, especially a religious one, and that their beliefs and practices are influenced by this.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.tr:
n. 英寻（长度单位）
v. 测深；推测；揣摩；搞懂；彻底了解
words.ex: The ship's anchor sank to a depth of ten fathoms.
words.ex_cn: 船的锚沉到了十英寻的深度。
words.en: If you cannot fathom something, you are unable to understand it, although you think carefully about it.

words.tr: n. 外延；本义；字面意思
words.ex: The denotation of 'dog' is a four-legged animal.
words.ex_cn: ‘狗’的外延是一种四条腿的动物。
words.en: The denotation of a word or phrase is its explicit or direct meaning, as distinguished from the ideas or meanings associated with it or suggested by it.

words.tr: v. 使慌乱；打扰；使担忧
words.ex: The loud noise didn't faze the experienced speaker.
words.ex_cn: v. 大声的噪音并没有打扰到这位有经验的演讲者。
words.en: To disturb or disconcert someone.

words.ex: He is culpable for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对这起事故负有责任。
words.en: If someone is culpable, they are responsible for something wrong or bad that has happened.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.ex: The light bulb has a thin filament.
words.ex_cn: 灯泡有一根细灯丝。
words.en: A filament is a very thin thread or fiber of natural or artificial material.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr:
adj. 僧侣的；修道院的；宁静简朴的
n. 僧侣；修道士
words.ex: He lives a monastic life in the old monastery.
words.ex_cn: 他在古老的修道院里过着修道般的生活。
words.en: Relating to monks, nuns, or others living under religious vows, or the buildings in which they live.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.ex: He added a codicil to his will, specifying additional bequests.
words.ex_cn: 他在遗嘱中添加了一个附录，指定了额外的遗产分配。
words.en: A codicil is an addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a will or part of one.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: His calmness is the antithesis of her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他的冷静是她愤怒的反面。
words.en: The antithesis of something is its exact opposite.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.ex: The government gave amnesty to political prisoners.
words.ex_cn: 政府向政治犯提供了赦免。
words.en: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of people by a government, especially for political offenses.

words.tr: adj. 教皇的；武断的；傲慢的
words.ex: He wore a pontifical robe during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿了一件教皇式的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Pope or to the office or authority of the Pope; having the pomp or dignity associated with high ecclesiastical office.

words.ex: He is a philanderer who dates many women.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢追逐很多女性的花花公子。
words.en: A man who readily enters into casual sexual relationships with women.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: The rain was a hindrance to the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨水对比赛造成了妨碍。
words.en: A hindrance is a person or thing that makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.ex: The dog grovelled on the ground to beg for food.
words.ex_cn: 狗趴在地上乞求食物。
words.en: If you grovel, you behave in a very submissive way in order to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done or to try to get someone to forgive you or do something for you.

words.tr: adj. 没有钱的；身无分文的；贫穷的
words.ex: The impecunious student had to rely on scholarships to continue his education.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的学生不得不依靠奖学金来继续他的学业。
words.en: If you describe someone as impecunious, you mean that they have very little money.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.ex: The school will rescind the rule next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将撤销这项规定。
words.en: If a government or a group of people in power rescind a law or agreement, they officially withdraw it and state that it is no longer valid.

words.tr: n. 输送；运输；财产让与；运输工具
words.ex: The conveyance of goods took three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输花了三天时间。
words.en: The act or process of transporting or carrying something from one place to another.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: The aboriginal people live in the forests of Australia.
words.ex_cn: 土著居民生活在澳大利亚的森林里。
words.en: An aboriginal person or thing is one that has been in a country or region from the earliest known times or from before the arrival of colonists.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
