words.ex: He was accused of being a philistine for his lack of interest in the arts.
words.ex_cn: 他因对艺术缺乏兴趣而被指责为没有文化教养的人。
words.en: A philistine is a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts, or who has no understanding of them.

words.tr:
adj. 告别的
n. 告别辞；告别演说
words.ex: He gave a valedictory speech at graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他在毕业典礼上发表了告别演讲。
words.en: A valedictory speech, letter, or performance is one that is intended as a goodbye.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.tr:
n. 试验；化验；定量分析
v. 试验；化验；定量分析
words.ex: The lab will assay the blood sample tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实验室明天将检测这个血液样本。
words.en: An assay is a test to determine the presence, absence, or quantity of one or more components.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr: v. 偷（尤指小的或不贵重的物品）
words.ex: He managed to filch a few apples from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他设法从市场上偷了几个苹果。
words.en: To steal something, especially something of little value or in a sneaky manner.

words.ex: She wore an amulet around her neck for protection.
words.ex_cn: 她脖子上戴着护身符以求保护。
words.en: An amulet is an object that is worn because it is believed to protect against evil, danger, or disease.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.tr: n. 长生不老药；仙丹妙药；
words.ex: The old wizard searched for an elixir to live forever.
words.ex_cn: 这位老巫师寻找一种能让人长生不老的药水。
words.en: An elixir is a magical or medicinal potion, especially one that is supposed to prolong life indefinitely.

words.ex: The typhoon destroyed many houses last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周的台风摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A typhoon is a very violent tropical storm that occurs in the western Pacific Ocean.

words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.tr: n. 知识分子（总称）；知识界；知识阶层
words.ex: The intelligentsia often debate the future of the country.
words.ex_cn: 知识分子经常辩论国家的未来。
words.en: The intelligentsia refers to the class of intellectuals regarded as possessing culture and political initiative.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.tr: adj. 娴静的；端庄的；假装矜持的
words.ex: She is a demure girl who never speaks loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个文静的女孩，从不大声说话。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a young woman, as demure, you mean they are quiet, shy, and behave so that they do not attract attention to themselves.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

words.ex: The syrup is very viscid and flows slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这种糖浆很粘稠，流动得很慢。
words.en: A viscid substance is thick and sticky.

words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.tr:
n. 退潮；衰退；减少
v. 退潮；衰退；减少
words.ex: The ebb of the tide left fish on the sand.
words.ex_cn: 退潮把鱼留在了沙滩上。
words.en: The movement of the tide out to sea.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: He is bellicose when he drinks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了时就好战。
words.en: Having or showing a tendency to argue or fight.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.ex: The serpentine road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯弯曲曲的路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: Something that is serpentine is curving and winding in shape, like a snake when it moves.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: He tries not to demean his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不贬低他的同学。
words.en: To demean someone or something means to cause them to lose their dignity or respect.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.ex: His charisma made everyone want to follow him.
words.ex_cn: 他的超凡魅力让所有人都想追随他。
words.en: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion in others.

words.ex: He glowered at the boy who broke his vase.
words.ex_cn: 他怒视着打碎他花瓶的那个男孩。
words.en: If you glower at someone or something, you look at them in an angry way.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.ex: They share intimacy through quiet talks at night.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过夜晚的安静交谈建立亲密感。
words.en: A close, familiar, and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship with another person or group.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr: adj. 青黑色的；苍白的；暴怒的
words.ex: His face turned livid after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的脸变得青黑色。
words.en: If you say that someone is livid, you mean that they are extremely angry.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.tr: adj. 五花八门的； v. “variegate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The garden has variegated flowers in many colors.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有五花八门的彩色花朵。
words.en: Having patches, stripes, or marks of different colors; diversified in appearance.

words.tr: n. 仲裁人；公断人；权威
words.ex: He is the arbiter of the dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场纠纷的仲裁者。
words.en: An arbiter is a person or agency officially appointed to settle a dispute.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr: n. 文雅；出身高贵；有风度
words.ex: His gentility made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的优雅使每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Gentility refers to the quality of being genteel, which involves showing the characteristics of polite society, such as refinement, grace, and good manners.

words.ex: His credulity made him an easy target for scams.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻信使他很容易成为诈骗的目标。
words.en: Credulity is a willingness to believe that something is real or true, especially when this is based on insufficient evidence.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: He was a liberator who freed the slaves.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位解放奴隶的解放者。
words.en: A liberator is someone who frees a place or a group of people from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression.

words.ex: The monster was just a figment of his imagination.
words.ex_cn: 那个怪物只是他想象出来的。
words.en: A figment is something that someone imagines or invents, often something that is not real.

words.tr: n. 突然发作；激发；阵发
words.ex: She experienced a paroxysm of coughing during the night.
words.ex_cn: 她在夜里经历了一次剧烈的咳嗽发作。
words.en: A paroxysm is a sudden attack or outburst of a particular emotion or activity.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.tr:
adj. 无法精确估量的
n. 无法估量的事物
words.ex: The reason for his silence is imponderable.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默的原因无法衡量。
words.en: An imponderable factor or element is one that cannot be precisely measured or assessed.

words.ex: The denizen of the forest knows all the paths.
words.ex_cn: 森林的居民知道所有的路。
words.en: A denizen of a particular place is someone who lives there or is often there.

words.tr: adj. 痉挛的；间歇的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had spasmodic coughing at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上有阵发性的咳嗽。
words.en: Something that is spasmodic happens suddenly and irregularly, often in short periods of time.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.tr:
adv. 有毛病地；出差错地；不合适地
adj. 有毛病的；出差错的；不合适的
words.ex: Something is amiss with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器有些不对劲。
words.en: If something is amiss, there is something wrong.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.ex: The detective used forensic evidence to solve the case.
words.ex_cn: 侦探使用法医证据破了案。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the application of scientific methods and techniques to the investigation of crime.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: adj. 屈从的；奴隶的；逢迎的
words.ex: He gave a servile answer to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他向老板给出了卑躬屈膝的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as servile, you disapprove of them because they are too eager to obey someone or do things for them.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.tr: v. 刺绣；绣（花）；加以渲染（或润色）
words.ex: She embroiders flowers on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上刺绣花朵。
words.en: To embroider means to decorate cloth or other material by sewing patterns or pictures on it with colored threads.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.ex: He was accused of heresy for rejecting the church's teachings.
words.ex_cn: 他因拒绝教会的教义而被指控为异端。
words.en: Heresy is a belief or opinion that is contrary to the orthodox religious doctrine, especially in Christianity.

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.tr: n. 海盗；不择手段的投机者；冒险家
words.ex: The buccaneer's ship was heavily armed.
words.ex_cn: 那名海盗的船装备精良。
words.en: A buccaneer is a person who sails the seas attacking and robbing ships, especially in the 17th and 18th centuries.

words.ex: He gave her a loud affirmation.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一个大声的肯定。
words.en: An affirmation is a statement or sign that something is true.

words.tr: adj. 繁重而累人的；艰苦的；使人精疲力尽的
words.ex: He ran a grueling marathon last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他上周日跑了一场艰苦的马拉松。
words.en: A grueling activity is extremely difficult and tiring, often continuing for a long time.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.ex: The nail protrudes from the wood.
words.ex_cn: 钉子从木头里凸出来。
words.en: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

words.ex: He abetted his friend to steal the car.
words.ex_cn: 他教唆朋友偷车。
words.en: To abet someone to do something wrong means to help or encourage them to do it.

words.tr: n. 流氓；无赖；小丑；（纸牌中的） J
words.ex: He was known as a cunning knave who would cheat anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以狡猾的无赖著称，会欺骗任何人。
words.en: A man who behaves dishonestly or unscrupulously.

words.ex: He gave a licentious speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上发表了一篇放荡不羁的演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person as licentious, you mean that they are very immoral in their sexual behavior.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.ex: He is learning theoretical physics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习理论物理。
words.en: A theoretical study or explanation is based on or uses the ideas and abstract principles of a subject, rather than the practical aspects or uses of it.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.tr: adj. 非典型的；不规则的
words.ex: He has an atypical way of solving problems.
words.ex_cn: 他解决问题的方式很不寻常。
words.en: Not representative of a type, group, or class; unusual or irregular.

words.ex: He does meditation every morning to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以放松。
words.en: Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.

words.tr:
n. 微弱的闪光；微弱的迹象；一丝
v. 发出微弱的闪光
words.ex: I saw a glimmer of light in the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 我在黑暗的房间里看到一丝光亮。
words.en: A glimmer is a faint, wavering light or a slight indication or trace of something.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
v. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
words.ex: She simpered at him, trying to catch his attention.
words.ex_cn: 她对他假笑，试图引起他的注意。
words.en: To smile in a silly or affected way, often to appear more attractive or to hide one's true feelings.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她有绘画的天赋。
words.en: If you have a flair for a particular activity, you have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: The kernel of the computer is the operating system.
words.ex_cn: 计算机的核心是操作系统。
words.en: The kernel of something such as a nut or a seed is the part inside the shell. The kernel of an idea or a theory is the central and most important part of it.

words.ex: The horse canter around the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野里慢跑。
words.en: If a horse canters, it moves at a speed that is slower than a gallop but faster than a trot.

words.tr:
n. 群；蜂群
v. 云集；充满
words.ex: Bees swarm around the flower.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂围绕着花朵成群飞舞。
words.en: A swarm is a large group of insects, especially bees, moving together. As a verb, it means to move in or form a swarm.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.tr: v. 敷衍；拖延；见风驶舵
words.ex: He decided to temporize until he had more information.
words.ex_cn: 他决定拖延时间，直到获得更多信息。
words.en: To temporize means to delay making a decision or giving a definite answer in order to gain time or avoid committing oneself.

words.ex: He felt resentment after being ignored by his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他被朋友忽视后感到怨恨。
words.en: Resentment is a feeling of anger or bitterness about something that you believe is unfair.

words.ex: The proliferation of bacteria causes the infection to spread.
words.ex_cn: 细菌的增殖导致感染扩散。
words.en: The rapid increase in the number or amount of something.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.tr: n. 装病以逃避责任者；装病的人
words.ex: He was accused of being a malingerer to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他因装病逃避工作而被指责。
words.en: Someone who pretends to be ill in order to avoid work or duty.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: He hates bigotry and speaks up for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨偏见，并为所有人发声。
words.en: Bigotry is the possession or expression of strong, unreasonable prejudices or opinions.

words.tr: n. 博学之士；大文豪；大学者
words.ex: He is a savant who can solve math problems instantly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位天才，能立即解决数学问题。
words.en: A savant is a person of profound or extensive learning; learned scholar.

words.tr: adj. 焦干的；干渴的； v. “parch”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The parched earth cracked under the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 焦干的土地在烈日下开裂了。
words.en: If something is parched, it is extremely dry, especially because of hot weather.

words.tr: n. 拱廊；有拱廊的街道；游乐中心
words.ex: The old arcade has stone pillars and a tiled roof.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的拱廊有石柱和瓦片屋顶。
words.en: A covered passage with arches along one or both sides.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.tr:
v. 轻快地掠过；突然换位；搬家
n. 掠过；迅速飞过；偷偷搬家
words.ex: The butterfly flits from flower to flower.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶在花朵间飞舞。
words.en: To move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.tr: v. 闪烁；发火花；焕发才智
words.ex: The diamonds on her necklace scintillated under the light.
words.ex_cn: 她项链上的钻石在灯光下闪闪发光。
words.en: To emit sparks or to sparkle; to twinkle; to be brilliant or lively in conversation or performance.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.tr:
n. （修道院等的）回廊；修道院
v. 关在…（修道院等）里；使…与世隔绝
words.ex: The monks lived a life of quiet contemplation in the cloister.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在修道院中过着宁静沉思的生活。
words.en: A cloister is a covered walk in a convent, monastery, college, or cathedral, typically with a wall on one side and a colonnade open to a quadrangle on the other.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.ex: The asperity of the terrain made the hike difficult.
words.ex_cn: 地形的粗糙使得徒步旅行变得困难。
words.en: If you say something with asperity, you say it in a harsh, severe way.

words.ex: The loud noise deranges the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让婴儿烦躁不安。
words.en: To derange something is to disturb the normal arrangement or functioning of it, often causing confusion or disorder.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.tr:
n. 箔；陪衬物
v. 阻止；挫败
words.ex: He used foil to wrap the sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他用锡纸包住了三明治。
words.en: To prevent someone from succeeding in their plans or intentions, especially by doing something clever or unexpected.

words.ex: The main reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The most important part or aspect of something.

words.tr: adj. 马虎的；敷衍了事的
words.ex: He gave a slipshod answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个敷衍的回答。
words.en: If something is slipshod, it is done in a careless or lazy way, without attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.tr: v. 迷惑；使迷惑不解；使糊涂
words.ex: The magic trick will mystify the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If you are mystified by something, you find it impossible to explain or understand.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: To freely transfer the possession of something to someone; to cause or allow someone to have something.

words.tr: n. 手段卑鄙的人；不择手段的律师
words.ex: He was known as a shyster who would do anything to win a case.
words.ex_cn: 他以不择手段赢得官司而臭名昭著。
words.en: A shyster is a person, especially a lawyer, who uses unethical or tricky methods in business or legal matters.

words.tr: v. 准许入学；被录取入学
words.ex: He will matriculate next fall.
words.ex_cn: 他将在明年秋天入学。
words.en: To matriculate means to enroll at a college or university, or to be accepted as a student by a college or university.

words.tr: n. 变色龙；见风使舵的人
words.ex: The chameleon changes color to hide.
words.ex_cn: 变色龙改变颜色来隐藏自己。
words.en: A chameleon is a type of lizard that can change the color of its skin in order to blend in with its surroundings.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: He has a thespian talent for acting.
words.ex_cn: 他有戏剧表演的天赋。
words.en: Relating to drama and the theater; an actor or actress.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.tr: v. 簸扬（谷）；分出好坏；筛选
words.ex: He winnows the wheat to remove the chaff.
words.ex_cn: 他用扬谷法去除麦子中的糠壳。
words.en: To winnow means to separate the grain from the chaff or to separate the good from the bad.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.ex: The summation of all the evidence was that he was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 所有证据的结论是他无罪。
words.en: A summation is a summary or the act of summarizing, especially in a legal context where it refers to the final argument made by an attorney at the end of a trial.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The pig eats from the wooden trough.
words.ex_cn: 猪从木槽里吃东西。
words.en: A long, narrow open container for animals to eat or drink from; a period of low economic activity.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的；令人憎恶的；糟糕的
words.ex: The weather was abominable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气糟糕透了。
words.en: If you describe something as abominable, you think that it is extremely unpleasant or bad.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: The dust formed an agglomeration on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘在地板上形成了结块。
words.en: An agglomeration is a mass or collection of things; especially a cluster of disparate elements.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.tr: adj. 可选择的；非强制的；
words.ex: The field trip is optional.
words.ex_cn: 这次郊游是可选的。
words.en: If something is optional, you can choose whether or not you do it or have it.

words.ex: The teacher showed connivance when students cheated.
words.ex_cn: 当学生作弊时，老师表现出默许。
words.en: Connivance is the act of conniving, especially by pretending not to notice something bad that is happening.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.ex: His fear of the dark is an atavism from our ancestors.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗的恐惧是我们祖先的返祖现象。
words.en: The reappearance in an organism of characteristics of some remote ancestor that have been absent in intervening generations.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.ex: The glass is transparent.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃是透明的。
words.en: If something is transparent, you can see through it.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr: adj. 过分挑剔的；苛求的
words.ex: He is finicky about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you say that someone is finicky, you mean that they are very difficult to please because they want everything to be exactly right.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；谄媚
n. 谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He was always the first to toady to the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他总是第一个拍老板马屁的人。
words.en: A toady is someone who flatters or ingratiates themselves with someone else in order to gain advantage.

words.ex: The portly man walks slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位胖胖的男人拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If you describe someone as portly, you mean that they are fat in a dignified way.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.ex: There is an exigency, so we must act now.
words.ex_cn: 情况紧急，我们必须立刻行动。
words.en: An exigency is a pressing or urgent situation or need that requires immediate action or attention.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.ex: The old tree had gnarled branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有布满节瘤的树枝。
words.en: If you describe someone's hands or fingers as gnarled, you mean that they are rough and twisted, often because they are old or have been used for a long time.

words.ex: The teacher berated the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To scold or criticize someone angrily.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.ex: The theocracy ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 神权政体以铁腕统治。
words.en: A theocracy is a form of government in which a deity is recognized as the supreme civil ruler, the deity's laws being interpreted by ecclesiastical authorities.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.tr: adj. 乏味的；无味的；枯燥的
words.ex: The movie was vapid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影乏味又无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vapid, you are criticizing them because they are dull and uninteresting.

words.tr: n. 殡仪业者；承办殡葬的人
words.ex: The mortician prepared the body for the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 殡葬业者为葬礼准备了遗体。
words.en: A mortician is a person whose job is to arrange and manage funerals.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.tr: n.  浮华；虚夸；炫耀；自负
words.ex: His pomposity often alienated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大使他经常疏远同事。
words.en: Pomposity is the quality of being pompous; self-importance.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.tr: v. 挑出（老弱动物）杀死；
words.ex: Farmers cull weak sheep to keep the herd healthy.
words.ex_cn: 农民挑出虚弱的羊杀死，以保持羊群健康。
words.en: To cull animals means to kill the weaker animals in a group in order to reduce their numbers or to prevent them from spreading disease.

words.tr: n. 凸起物；突出部分；结节；瘤
words.ex: The rock has a small protuberance on top.
words.ex_cn: 这块石头顶部有一个小突起。
words.en: A protuberance is a part that sticks out from the surface of something.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.ex: He dissimulated his anger to keep the peace.
words.ex_cn: 他掩饰了自己的愤怒以维持和平。
words.en: To dissimulate means to hide your real feelings, character, or intentions.

words.tr: adj. 对（享乐）感到厌倦的；（因司空见惯而）无动于衷的
words.ex: He is blase about the new phone because he has one every year.
words.ex_cn: 他对新手机无动于衷，因为他每年都换一部。
words.en: If you describe someone as blasé, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.tr: n. 派系；小集团；小圈子
words.ex: She found it hard to break into the clique at school.
words.ex_cn: 她发现很难融入学校的小圈子。
words.en: A clique is a small group of people who spend their time together and do not allow others to join them.

words.ex: The team showed great camaraderie during the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队在比赛中展现了深厚的友爱。
words.en: A feeling of good friendship among the people in a group.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.ex: The virulent virus spread quickly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种剧毒的病毒迅速在小镇上传播。
words.en: A virulent disease or poison is extremely powerful and dangerous.

words.ex: The gale knocked down several trees.
words.ex_cn: 大风刮倒了几棵树。
words.en: A gale is a very strong wind.

words.tr:
adj. 同源的；同语系的
n. 同家族的人；同源词
words.ex: English 'mother' and German 'Mutter' are cognate.
words.ex_cn: 英语的 'mother' 和德语的 'Mutter' 是同源词。
words.en: Cognate refers to words or languages that have a common origin or are related in their development.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.tr: n. 仓库；贮藏室；存放处；智囊
words.ex: He saves his code in a GitHub repository.
words.ex_cn: 他把代码保存在 GitHub 仓库中。
words.en: A repository is a place where something is stored or can be found.

words.tr: n. 恩人；捐助者；赠送者
words.ex: The benefactor gave money to the school.
words.ex_cn: 资助人捐钱给学校。
words.en: A benefactor is a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.

words.ex: The feral cat lives in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 这只野生的猫生活在森林里。
words.en: A feral animal is a domestic animal that has returned to the wild, or is the offspring of such animals, and is not socialized to humans.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.tr: adj. 该诅咒的；恶劣的；极坏的
words.ex: The food was execrable.
words.ex_cn: 这食物糟糕透顶。
words.en: If you describe something as execrable, you mean that it is extremely bad or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.ex: The loud music was obnoxious and made everyone leave.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐非常讨厌，让所有人都离开了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as obnoxious, you think that they are very unpleasant because of being aggressive, loud, or offensive.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.tr: n. 肮脏；污秽；恶劣条件
words.ex: The family lived in squalor with no clean water.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭生活在肮脏的环境中，没有干净的水。
words.en: A state of being extremely dirty and unpleasant, especially as a result of poverty or neglect.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: n. 代理人；特工；经纪人；（药）剂；动因；
words.ex: The real estate agent helped them buy a house.
words.ex_cn: 房地产代理人帮助他们买了一所房子。
words.en: An agent is a person who acts on behalf of another person or group.

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.tr: v. 解开(~ sth. out)；使更复杂(~ sth. up)
words.ex: She raveled the tangled yarn out slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她慢慢地把缠绕的毛线解开。
words.en: To ravel means to tangle or untangle threads or fibers, or to become tangled or untangled. It can also refer to the process of separating the threads of a woven or knitted fabric, or to confuse or complicate a situation.

words.tr:
v. 马嘶；轻声嘶鸣
n. 马嘶；嘶声
words.ex: The horse whinny loudly when it sees the farmer.
words.ex_cn: 马一看到农夫就嘶鸣。
words.en: A whinny is a gentle, high-pitched sound made by a horse, often as a greeting or to express excitement.

words.ex: The diminution of water in the lake is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 湖中水量的减少是显而易见的。
words.en: A diminution of something is its reduction in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr: n. 不安；良心之谴责；疑虑；“qualm”的复数
words.ex: He had no qualms about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎毫无愧疚。
words.en: If you have no qualms about doing something, you are not worried that it may be wrong in some way.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.tr: n. 违禁品；禁运品；走私货
words.ex: The police seized a large amount of contraband in the raid.
words.ex_cn: 警方在突击搜查中查获了大量走私货。
words.en: Goods that are illegally imported or exported.

words.tr: n. 怜悯；悲情；哀婉；凄楚
words.ex: The movie filled us with pathos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让我们充满感动。
words.en: Pathos is a quality in a work of art or literature that evokes feelings of pity or sadness.

words.ex: He tried to expiate his guilt by helping the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过帮助穷人来赎罪。
words.en: If you expiate guilty feelings or bad behaviour, you do something to show that you are sorry for what you have done.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: It is the president's prerogative to make final decisions.
words.ex_cn: 做最终决定是总统的特权。
words.en: A prerogative is a right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.

words.ex: She wrote a letter to condole with him on his loss.
words.ex_cn: 她写了一封信，对他的损失表示慰问。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a misfortune or loss.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophistry, making it difficult to discern the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，让人难以分辨真相。
words.en: Sophistry is the use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving.

words.ex: The math proof requires rigor.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学证明需要严谨。
words.en: Rigor is a situation in which people are made to follow rules in a very strict way.

words.ex: The cost of lunch was incidental to the main expense.
words.ex_cn: 午餐的费用是主要开销的附带部分。
words.en: If one thing is incidental to another, it is less important than the other thing or is not a major part of it.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；空洞的；无意义的
words.ex: His inane comments made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他无聊的评论让每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone's comments or ideas as inane, you mean they are very silly or stupid.

words.tr:
v. 猛扭；扭伤；挣脱
n. 扳手；扳钳；（离别的）痛苦
words.ex: He wrenched the door open with all his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他用尽全力猛扭门，把它打开了。
words.en: A wrench is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, pipes, etc. It can also refer to a sudden violent twist or pull, or a feeling of sadness or distress caused by separation.

words.ex: His suavity made everyone feel comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的温文尔雅让每个人都感到舒适。
words.en: Suavity is the quality of being suave, which means being smoothly agreeable and polite.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: The milk turned rancid after being left out.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶被放在外面后变酸了。
words.en: If food is rancid, it tastes or smells bad because it is no longer fresh.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.ex: He has a slight cold.
words.ex_cn: 他有点轻微的感冒。
words.en: A slight change, difference, or action is not very great or important.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.tr: adj. 无法触及的；摸不着的；难解的
words.ex: The concept of infinity is often considered impalpable.
words.ex_cn: 无限的概念常常被认为是难以理解的。
words.en: Impalpable means something that cannot be perceived by touch or is very difficult to understand or define.

words.ex: The students did a frog dissection in biology class.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在生物课上做了青蛙解剖。
words.en: The act of cutting something apart to examine its structure, typically in a scientific context.

words.ex: The rendition of the song by the singer moved everyone.
words.ex_cn: 歌手对这首歌的演出打动了所有人。
words.en: A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.

words.tr: adj. 朦胧的；模糊的；不清楚的
words.ex: The sky looks hazy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上天空看起来雾蒙蒙的。
words.en: If it is hazy, it is not clear because there is a lot of mist, smoke, or dust in the air.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.ex: The coach checks the roster before every game.
words.ex_cn: 教练在每场比赛前检查名单。
words.en: A roster is a list which gives details of the members of a team, organization, or group, and the times or order in which they are to perform a particular duty.

words.ex: The vendor sells fresh fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这个商贩在市场卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A vendor is a person or company that sells goods or services.

words.tr: n. 圆形剧场；竞技场；梯形教室
words.ex: The students watched a play in the old amphitheater.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在旧的圆形剧场里观看了戏剧。
words.en: An amphitheater is a large open area surrounded by rows of seats sloping upwards. Amphitheaters were used in ancient Greece and Rome for public entertainments.

words.ex: He practices abstinence from alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他戒酒。
words.en: The practice of restraining oneself from indulging in something, typically alcohol or sex.

words.tr: adj. 爱开玩笑的；乱引人发笑的
words.ex: He gave a facetious answer when asked about his age.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到年龄时，他给出了一个开玩笑的回答。
words.en: If you say that someone is being facetious, you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

words.ex: He went on an odyssey to find his lost brother.
words.ex_cn: 他踏上了一段寻找失散兄弟的漫长旅程。
words.en: An odyssey is a long and eventful or adventurous journey or experience.

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.ex: The rainwater collects in a large cistern.
words.ex_cn: 雨水收集在一个大水箱里。
words.en: A cistern is a container for storing water, especially one that is part of a system for supplying water to a building or for collecting rainwater.

words.ex: He works in a small cubicle at the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室的一个小隔间里工作。
words.en: A cubicle is a small space or compartment that is partitioned off, especially one in which someone works or studies.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: He was punished for plagiarism in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他因论文剽窃而受到惩罚。
words.en: Plagiarism is the practice of using or copying someone else's idea or work and pretending that you thought of it or created it.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.tr: n. 天真无邪的少女；扮演天真少女的女演员
words.ex: She played the ingenue in the romantic comedy.
words.ex_cn: 她在那部浪漫喜剧中扮演了天真无邪的少女。
words.en: An ingenue is a young woman, especially in a play or film, who is innocent and wholesome.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.tr:
adj. 无力偿付债务的；破产的
n. 破产者；无力偿还者
words.ex: The company went insolvent after years of financial mismanagement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在多年的财务管理不善后破产了。
words.en: If a person or organization is insolvent, they do not have enough money to pay their debts.

words.ex: The insularity of Japan affects its cultural traditions.
words.ex_cn: 日本的岛国特性影响了它的文化传统。
words.en: The state of being isolated or detached from others, often resulting in a narrow or limited perspective.

words.tr: adj. 回顾的；回想的；溯及既往的
words.ex: He made a retrospective look at his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回顾了自己的童年。
words.en: A retrospective is an exhibition or compilation showing the development of an artist's work over a period of time. It can also refer to a look back at past events or situations.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.tr: adj. 不合适的；不相称的；不协调的；
words.ex: His funny hat was incongruous with the formal suit.
words.ex_cn: 他的滑稽帽子与正式西装不搭配。
words.en: Something that is incongruous is strange when considered together with other aspects of a situation.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.tr:
adj. 装腔作势的
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地说；“mince”的现在分词
words.ex: He is mincing garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把大蒜剁碎做酱汁。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as mincing, you mean that they are behaving in a way that is intended to appear elegant or refined, but seems artificial and silly.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: The obstetrician helped the baby be born.
words.ex_cn: 产科医生帮助婴儿出生。
words.en: An obstetrician is a doctor who specializes in pregnancy, childbirth, and a woman's reproductive system.

words.ex: His haughtiness made others avoid him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人躲着他。
words.en: Haughtiness is the quality of being arrogantly superior and disdainful.

words.ex: The child looked through the kaleidoscope and laughed.
words.ex_cn: 孩子透过万花筒看，笑了。
words.en: A kaleidoscope is a toy consisting of a tube containing mirrors and pieces of colored glass or paper, whose reflections produce changing patterns when the tube is rotated. It can also refer to a constantly changing pattern or sequence of elements.

words.ex: He always follows the maxim 'work hard, play hard'.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循‘努力工作，尽情玩耍’这一信条。
words.en: A maxim is a short, easily remembered expression of a basic principle, general truth, or rule of conduct.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr:
n. 寿衣；裹尸布；覆盖物
v. 覆盖；遮蔽
words.ex: The body was wrapped in a white shroud.
words.ex_cn: 遗体被裹在一件白色的寿衣里。
words.en: A shroud is a cloth which is used for wrapping a dead body. It can also refer to something that covers, hides, or protects.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.tr: v. 施以催眠术；迷住；迷惑
words.ex: The dancer mesmerized the crowd with her slow movements.
words.ex_cn: 舞者用她缓慢的动作对观众施以催眠术。
words.en: If you are mesmerized by something, you are so interested in it or so attracted to it that you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverize the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverize something means to crush it into a fine powder or to defeat someone or something completely.

words.tr:
adj. 断音的；不连贯的
adv. 断音地；不连贯地
n. 断奏；断续的一段音乐
words.ex: The piano played staccato notes.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴弹奏了断奏的音符。
words.en: In music, staccato is a method of playing notes in a detached, separated manner, as opposed to legato.

words.tr:
n. 嘈杂声；喧闹声
v. 喧闹；喋喋不休地说
words.ex: The children made a loud din in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里发出很大的嘈杂声。
words.en: A din is a loud, unpleasant, and prolonged noise.

words.tr: adj. 神圣化的； 受崇敬的
words.ex: The hallowed ground is where the heroes rest.
words.ex_cn: 那片神圣的土地是英雄们安息的地方。
words.en: Something that is hallowed is respected and admired, usually because it is old, important, or has a good reputation.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.ex: The map has an indicative arrow to show the way.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图上有一个指示方向的箭头。
words.en: If one thing is indicative of another, it suggests what the other thing is likely to be.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr:
v. 熔炼；冶炼
v. 嗅；闻；散发气味；察觉；“smell”的过去式和过去分词
n. 胡瓜鱼
words.ex: They smelt iron ore to make steel.
words.ex_cn: 他们熔炼铁矿石来制造钢铁。
words.en: To smelt means to extract metal from ore by a process involving heating and melting.

words.ex: The music is evocative of childhood memories.
words.ex_cn: 这音乐唤起了童年的回忆。
words.en: If you describe something as evocative, you mean that it is good or interesting because it produces pleasant memories, ideas, emotions, and responses in people.

words.ex: Salt is soluble in water.
words.ex_cn: 盐可以溶于水。
words.en: A substance that is soluble can be dissolved in a liquid.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr: adj. 无产阶级的；n. 无产者
words.ex: The proletarian worked long hours in the factory.
words.ex_cn: 普罗在工厂里长时间工作。
words.en: A proletarian is a member of the proletariat, the class of wage-earners in a capitalist society whose only possession of significant material value is their labor-power.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.ex: The forest shows regeneration after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 森林在火灾后显示出再生。
words.en: The process of renewal, restoration, and growth that makes cells, organisms, and ecosystems resilient to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.tr: n. 小花饰；简介；（表演）片段
words.ex: She drew a small vignette on the corner of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 她在信的角落画了一个小花饰。
words.en: A vignette is a brief evocative description, account, or episode.

words.ex: He was born in August.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在八月。
words.en: August is the eighth month of the Gregorian calendar, following July and preceding September.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.tr: adj. 偶然的；外来的；不定的
words.ex: The plant grew adventitious roots from its stem.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物从茎上长出了不定根。
words.en: Adventitious means happening or carried on according to chance rather than design or inherent nature.

words.ex: He feels panic in small rooms because of claustrophobia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为幽闭恐惧症在小房间里感到恐慌。
words.en: A morbid fear of being closed in a confined space.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.tr: adj. 违背良心的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: The prices they were charging were unconscionable.
words.ex_cn: 他们收取的价格是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unconscionable, you mean that it is morally unacceptable, often because it is too large, too extreme, or too severe.

words.tr: n. 吝啬鬼；小气鬼；守财奴
words.ex: He was known as a tightwad who never spent a penny unnecessarily.
words.ex_cn: 他以吝啬鬼闻名，从不花不必要的钱。
words.en: A tightwad is a person who is very reluctant to spend money; a miser.

words.ex: The burly man carried two heavy boxes easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个健壮的男人轻松地搬了两个重箱子。
words.en: A burly person is big and strong.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.ex: The car remained static at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在红灯前静止不动。
words.en: Something that is static does not move or change.

words.ex: He will append his name to the list.
words.ex_cn: 他将在名单上加上他的名字。
words.en: To add something to the end of a piece of writing.

words.tr: adj. 极甜的；过分甜的；故作多情的；奉承的；过于亲近的
words.ex: The cake tasted too saccharine.
words.ex_cn: 这块蛋糕尝起来太甜了。
words.en: Excessively sweet or sentimental.

words.tr:
n. 恶棍；无赖；流氓
v. 草率地做
words.ex: He was always getting into trouble, but he was a lovable scamp.
words.ex_cn: 他总是惹麻烦，但他是个讨人喜欢的小流氓。
words.en: A scamp is a person, especially a child, who is mischievous in a likable or amusing way.

words.tr:
n. 漩涡；涡流
v. 起漩涡；旋转；杂乱无章地移动
words.ex: The river has a small eddy near the rock.
words.ex_cn: 河里石头附近有一个小漩涡。
words.en: An eddy is a circular movement of water, air, or smoke that is different from the main current.

words.ex: His frugality helped him save money for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的节俭让他多年都存下了钱。
words.en: Frugality is the quality of being careful with money or food, so that you only spend what is necessary.

words.ex: The auctioneer brought the gavel down with a decisive strike.
words.ex_cn: 拍卖师果断地敲下小木槌。
words.en: A gavel is a small wooden hammer that a person in charge of a meeting or an auction hits against a wooden block to call for attention or order.

words.ex: The factory dumped slag near the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂把矿渣倒在河边。
words.en: Slag is the glass-like by-product left over after a desired metal has been separated (i.e., smelted) from its raw ore. Slag is usually a mixture of metal oxides and silicon dioxide. However, slags can contain metal sulfides and elemental metals.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.ex: She is the epitome of kindness.
words.ex_cn: 她是善良的典型。
words.en: A person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The horror movie showed a man being dismembered.
words.ex_cn: 那部恐怖电影展示了一名男子被肢解。
words.en: To dismember means to cut, tear, or pull the limbs from a body.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.tr: n. 骗子；江湖骗子；诈骗犯
words.ex: The swindler tricked old people with fake promises.
words.ex_cn: 这个骗子用虚假的承诺欺骗了老人。
words.en: A swindler is someone who swindles, that is, someone who cheats or tricks someone else out of money or property.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.ex: The snake sloughs its skin every year.
words.ex_cn: 蛇每年都会蜕皮。
words.en: A slough is an area of soft, muddy ground, especially a marshy area by a river or lake. As a verb, it means to shed or cast off a layer of dead skin, a shell, or an old layer of tissue.

words.ex: Farmers grow corn as a crop.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植玉米作为农作物。
words.en: A crop is a plant such as wheat, potatoes, or cotton that is grown in large quantities by farmers.

words.ex: He works on a nautical chart.
words.ex_cn: 他正在使用一张航海图。
words.en: Nautical means relating to ships, sailing, or navigation at sea.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.tr: adv. 成碎片地；弄碎地；分离地
words.ex: The kingdom was torn asunder by civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个王国因内战而被撕裂。
words.en: Into parts or pieces; apart.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷不醒的；不省人事的；困乏的
words.ex: The man became comatose after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这个人陷入了昏迷。
words.en: If someone is comatose, they are in a coma and are not conscious.

words.ex: The detonation of the bomb caused widespread destruction.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹的爆炸造成了大范围的破坏。
words.en: A detonation is a large or powerful explosion.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.ex: The music enraptured the whole audience.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让整个观众着迷。
words.en: To fill someone with great delight or joy.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.tr: v. 深思熟虑；慎重考虑
words.ex: He cogitates before he answers the question.
words.ex_cn: 他在回答问题之前会深思。
words.en: To think deeply about something; to ponder or meditate.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: He affixed a stamp to the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把邮票贴在信封上。
words.en: To attach, fasten, or join something to something else.

words.ex: Applications arrived in an avalanche after the job posting.
words.ex_cn: 职位发布后，申请纷至沓来。
words.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow, ice, and rocks that falls quickly down the side of a mountain.

words.ex: He wrote a manifesto to explain his ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份宣言来解释他的观点。
words.en: A manifesto is a written statement of the beliefs, aims, and policies of an organization, especially a political party.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
