words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽拙劣的模仿；嘲弄；歪曲
v. 滑稽化；嘲弄
words.ex: The trial was a travesty of justice.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是对正义的嘲弄。
words.en: If you describe something as a travesty of another thing, you mean that it is a very bad representation of that other thing.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；精神错乱状态的
words.ex: The demented man laughed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神失常的男人在街上大声笑。
words.en: Someone who is demented behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way because they are mentally ill.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.tr: v. 详细说明；详细解释
words.ex: He will explicate the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 他将解释这首诗的含义。
words.en: To explicate something means to explain it in detail, making it clear and understandable.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.ex: Reindeer live in the tundra near the North Pole.
words.ex_cn: 驯鹿生活在北极附近的苔原上。
words.en: A tundra is a vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.

words.ex: The cessation of rain allowed us to go outside.
words.ex_cn: 雨停了，我们就能出去了。
words.en: The fact or process of ending or being brought to an end.

words.ex: The thief tried to waylay the man on the dark street.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图在黑暗的街道上拦住那个男人。
words.en: To lie in wait for and attack from ambush

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.ex: The cool water helped to slake his thirst.
words.ex_cn: 清凉的水帮助他解渴。
words.en: If you slake a thirst, desire, or need, you satisfy it.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.tr: adj. 近视眼的；缺乏远见的
words.ex: He is myopic and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If you describe someone as myopic, you are critical of them because they seem unable to realize that their actions might have negative consequences.

words.ex: Bears hibernate in winter to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠以保存能量。
words.en: To spend the winter in a dormant state.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.ex: The school has draconian rules about phone use.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校对手机使用有极其严厉的规定。
words.en: Draconian laws or measures are extremely harsh and severe.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: The bird uses mimicry to copy other animals' sounds.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟通过模仿来复制其他动物的声音。
words.en: The action or art of imitating someone or something, especially in order to entertain or ridicule.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: He found nirvana after meditating for years.
words.ex_cn: 他经过多年的冥想后找到了涅槃。
words.en: In Buddhism, nirvana is the ultimate state of liberation from suffering and the cycle of rebirth.

words.tr:
v. 打滚；翻滚
n. 混乱的一堆
words.ex: The box was full of a welter of old toys.
words.ex_cn: 盒子里堆满了各种旧玩具。
words.en: A welter is a state of general confusion or disorder. It can also refer to a heavy or confused mass of something, such as a welter of papers.

words.ex: They shouted recrimination at each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此大声指责。
words.en: Recrimination is the act of accusing someone who has accused you of something.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.tr: n. 火把；燃烧的木柴；煽动者
words.ex: He is a firebrand who speaks loudly against injustice.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个大声反对不公的激进分子。
words.en: A firebrand is a person who is passionate about a particular cause, often inciting others to action or rebellion.

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.ex: The ball followed a smooth trajectory.
words.ex_cn: 球沿着一条平滑的轨迹飞行。
words.en: The path followed by a projectile flying or an object moving under the action of given forces.

words.ex: The courier delivered the letter quickly.
words.ex_cn: 信使迅速送来了这封信。
words.en: A courier is a person or company that delivers messages, packages, and mail.

words.tr:
n. 小人国的人；小东西
adj. 小的；矮小的
words.ex: The furniture in the dollhouse was all lilliputian, perfect for the tiny inhabitants.
words.ex_cn: 娃娃屋里的家具都是小人国的，非常适合那些小居民。
words.en: Very small; relating to Lilliput or its inhabitants; trivial or petty.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的
words.ex: The psychic claimed to have preternatural abilities.
words.ex_cn: 这位通灵者声称自己拥有超自然的能力。
words.en: Beyond what is normal or natural; supernatural.

words.tr:
v. 哄笑；大笑
n. 哄笑；大笑
words.ex: The audience broke into a guffaw when the comedian slipped on stage.
words.ex_cn: 喜剧演员在舞台上滑倒时，观众哄堂大笑。
words.en: A guffaw is a very loud laugh.

words.tr: n. 区别；区分；优等评分；
words.ex: There is a clear distinction between right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 对与错之间有明显的区别。
words.en: A distinction is a difference or contrast between similar things or people.

words.ex: He caught a scad while fishing at the pier.
words.ex_cn: 他在码头钓鱼时捕到一条竹荚鱼。
words.en: A large number or amount of something.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.tr: n. 打油诗；蹩脚诗；歪诗
words.ex: He wrote doggerel for fun.
words.ex_cn: 他为了好玩写了打油诗。
words.en: Doggerel is a form of verse that is irregular in rhythm and often intentionally silly or trivial in content.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.ex: His voice sounds raspy after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他大喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: A raspy voice or sound is unpleasantly rough.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.tr:
v. 吹拂；（随风）飘荡；使飘荡
n. 一股（在空气中飘荡的味或烟）；风信旗；飘荡
words.ex: The smell of bread wafted from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味从厨房里飘来。
words.en: If sounds or smells waft through the air, or if something such as a light wind wafts them, they move gently through the air.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.ex: Good teachers edify their students with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 好老师用智慧启发学生。
words.en: To edify someone means to improve their mind or character by teaching them something.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.ex: The contortion bent her body into a small box.
words.ex_cn: 这个柔术演员把身体弯进了一个小盒子里。
words.en: A contortion is a twisted or bent shape or position, often of the body.

words.tr: n. 欢腾；欢欣鼓舞；欢庆
words.ex: There was a lot of jubilation when the team won the championship.
words.ex_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，人们欢呼雀跃。
words.en: A feeling of great happiness and triumph.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.tr:
n. 烤架；铁格子
v. 烧烤；拷问
words.ex: He cooked the burgers on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他用烤架烤了汉堡。
words.en: To cook food on a metal frame over a fire, or a metal frame used for cooking food in this way.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: The teacher asked students to annotate the text with notes.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们在文本上做注释。
words.en: To add notes or comments to a text or diagram, providing explanation or criticism.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.tr: v. 使慌张；使窘迫；使不安
words.ex: The sudden noise disconcerted her.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让她感到不安。
words.en: If something disconcerts you, it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: The colors in the rainbow cover a wide spectrum.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹中的颜色覆盖了广泛的范围。
words.en: A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing, often a range of colors, ideas, or opinions.

words.tr:
v. 说孩子气的话；说半截话；闲扯；多嘴多舌
n. 孩子般颠三倒四的话；连续而无意义的声音；废话
words.ex: She prattled on about her new dress.
words.ex_cn: 她喋喋不休地谈论她的新裙子。
words.en: If someone prattles on about something, they talk for a long time in a boring or silly way because they keep talking about unimportant things.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.tr: adj. 节日的；喜庆的；欢乐的
words.ex: The streets are festive during Christmas.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞节期间，街道上充满了节日气氛。
words.en: Something that is festive is special, colorful, or exciting, especially because it is connected with a festival or celebration.

words.tr:
v. 藐视；轻视；嘲笑
n. 嘲弄；轻视
words.ex: He flouts the rules every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都无视规则。
words.en: If you flout something such as a law, an order, or an accepted way of behaving, you deliberately do not obey it or follow it.

words.ex: His opening gambit was a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他的开场白是一个简单的问题。
words.en: A gambit is a clever action in a game or other situation that is intended to achieve an advantage and usually involves taking a risk.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；无礼的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His churlish behavior at the meeting was uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的粗鲁行为是完全没有必要的。
words.en: If someone is churlish, they are rude, bad-tempered, and impolite.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 恶心的；欲吐的；稍感紧张的；略有不安的
words.ex: He feels queasy after eating too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖果后感到恶心。
words.en: If you feel queasy, you feel slightly sick or uncomfortable, especially because you are nervous or worried.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr: n. .高级教士；职位甚高的教士
words.ex: The prelate delivered a sermon on the importance of charity.
words.ex_cn: 这位高级教士在布道中讲述了慈善的重要性。
words.en: A prelate is a high-ranking member of the clergy, such as a bishop, who has authority over other clergy and often over a specific area.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The famous artist took her young protege under her wing.
words.ex_cn: 这位著名艺术家收这位年轻后辈为徒。
words.en: A protégé is a person who is guided and supported by an older and more experienced or influential person.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.tr: adj. 两院制的；有参众两院的
words.ex: The country has a bicameral parliament.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个两院制议会。
words.en: A bicameral legislature is one that is divided into two separate assemblies, chambers, or houses.

words.ex: The soda shows effervescence when poured.
words.ex_cn: 汽水倒出来时会冒泡。
words.en: Effervescence is the process of bubbles forming in a liquid, which is often associated with the release of gas. It can also describe a lively and enthusiastic quality in a person or atmosphere.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The hikers got stuck in a quagmire near the river.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在河边陷入了一片沼泽地。
words.en: A quagmire is a difficult, complicated, or unpleasant situation that is hard to escape from.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.ex: The movie caused hilarity among the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众们哄堂大笑。
words.en: Hilarity is great amusement and laughter.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: The government decided to divest the company of its assets.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定剥夺该公司的资产。
words.en: If you divest someone of power, rights, or authority, you take those things away from them. If you divest yourself of something that you own or are responsible for, you get rid of it or stop being responsible for it.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.ex: He is a dutiful son who helps his parents every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个孝顺的儿子，每天帮助父母。
words.en: Someone who is dutiful is careful to do the things that they are expected to do.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.tr:
adj. 持不同意见的
n. 意见不同的人；持不同政见者
words.ex: The dissident spoke out against the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位持不同政见者公开反对政府。
words.en: A dissident is a person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.

words.ex: The centripetal force keeps the ball moving in a circle.
words.ex_cn: 向心力使球保持圆周运动。
words.en: Moving or tending to move toward a center.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；像尸体的；枯槁的
words.ex: His cadaverous appearance frightened the children.
words.ex_cn: 他那尸体般的惨白面容吓坏了孩子们。
words.en: If you describe someone as cadaverous, you mean they are extremely thin and pale.

words.ex: His wrath scared everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒吓到了房间里的每个人。
words.en: Extreme anger.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.tr:
adj. 收敛性的；止血的；辛辣的；严厉的；涩的
n. 收敛剂； 止血药
words.ex: The astringent lotion helps reduce swelling.
words.ex_cn: 这种收敛性的爽肤水有助于减轻肿胀。
words.en: An astringent substance causes the contraction of body tissues, typically used to reduce bleeding from minor abrasions or as a skin toner.

words.ex: The movie shows an apocalyptic future after a big war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影描绘了大战之后预示未来灾难的景象。
words.en: Relating to or predicting the end of the world, especially as described in the Bible.

words.ex: The monk recited the Beatitudes during the service.
words.ex_cn: 修道士在仪式中背诵了至福经。
words.en: Supreme blessedness or happiness.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 驱（魔）；除去（痛苦的想法等）
words.ex: The priest tried to exorcise the demon from the house.
words.ex_cn: 牧师试图将恶魔从房子里驱逐出去。
words.en: To exorcise means to drive out or attempt to drive out (a supposed evil spirit) from a person or place.

words.tr: v. 把…打扮得俗里俗气
words.ex: She bedizened herself with gaudy jewelry.
words.ex_cn: 她用俗艳的珠宝打扮自己。
words.en: To bedizen means to dress or decorate in a showy or gaudy manner.

words.ex: He is facing litigation over the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他因合同问题面临诉讼。
words.en: Litigation is the process of taking legal action or bringing a lawsuit in a court of law.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr: adj. 带酸味的；微酸的；尖刻刻薄的
words.ex: The lemonade was acidulous and sharp.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬水酸得刺口。
words.en: Slightly sour or sharp in taste or manner.

words.tr:
n. 亲属；血缘关系
adj. 同源的；类似的
words.ex: He visited his kindred during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他在假期里探望了他的亲属。
words.en: If two people or things are kindred, they are similar in some way, often because they are related.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；开玩笑的；闹着玩的
words.ex: He told a jocose joke to make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个幽默的笑话来让大家笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jocose, you mean that they are playful and humorous.

words.tr: n. 复制本；摹本；仿制品；传真
words.ex: He sent a facsimile of the document to his office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件的传真发到了办公室。
words.en: An exact copy of a document, picture, or piece of writing, especially one that has been made by a machine.

words.tr: adj. 无表情的（面孔）；表情冷淡的
words.ex: He delivered the punchline with a deadpan expression.
words.ex_cn: 他用面无表情的表情说出了笑点。
words.en: If you describe someone as deadpan, you mean that they appear serious and do not show emotion in their face or voice, even when they are joking or teasing.

words.ex: The king sent an emissary to talk to the neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 国王派了一名使者去与邻国交谈。
words.en: An emissary is a person who is sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.

words.ex: The difference between the two values is infinitesimal.
words.ex_cn: 这两个值之间的差异极微。
words.en: Something that is infinitesimal is extremely small.

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr: adj. 没有减轻的；十足的；绝对的
words.ex: The criticism was unmitigated and harsh.
words.ex_cn: 批评是全然的严厉。
words.en: If you describe something as unmitigated, you are emphasizing that it is completely bad or good, without any qualification.

words.ex: The brindled cat blended into the shadows.
words.ex_cn: 这只有斑纹的猫融入了阴影中。
words.en: Having a grey or brownish coat streaked or spotted with a darker color.

words.tr:
n. 影射；暗指
v. 旁敲侧击地表达；含沙射影
words.ex: He made an innuendo about her being late.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她迟到了。
words.en: An indirect or subtle, usually derogatory implication in expression; an insinuation.

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.tr: adj. 不奸猾的；厚道的；坦率的
words.ex: He is a guileless boy who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个纯真无邪的男孩，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as guileless, you mean that they behave openly and truthfully and do not try to deceive people.

words.ex: The swamp was filled with a thick miasma.
words.ex_cn: 沼泽里充满了浓重的瘴气。
words.en: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy smell or atmosphere.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: He felt uncomfortable with the adulation from his fans.
words.ex_cn: 他对于粉丝们的盲目崇拜感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive admiration or praise.

words.ex: The accident caused immobility in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故导致他的腿无法动弹。
words.en: The state of not being able to move or be moved.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.tr: v. 骚扰；烦扰；屡次侵扰
words.ex: He harasses his coworkers with loud jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他用大声的笑话骚扰他的同事。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.ex: He swore allegiance to his country.
words.ex_cn: 他向自己的国家宣誓效忠。
words.en: Loyalty or commitment to a superior or to a group or cause.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.tr: v. 打滚；躺卧；（船）颠簸；沉湎
words.ex: The pig wallow in the mud.
words.ex_cn: 猪在泥里打滚。
words.en: If you say that someone is wallowing in an unpleasant situation, you are criticizing them for being deliberately unhappy.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.tr: adj. 不讨人喜欢的；不吸引人的；
words.ex: He has an unprepossessing appearance, but he is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他外表不讨人喜欢，但他非常善良。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unprepossessing, you mean that they look rather plain or ordinary, and not at all impressive or attractive.

words.ex: The farmer piled up fodder for the cows.
words.ex_cn: 农夫为奶牛堆了一堆饲料。
words.en: Fodder is food that is given to cows, horses, and other animals.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.ex: The school will curtail recess time during exams.
words.ex_cn: 学校在考试期间将缩短课间休息时间。
words.en: If you curtail something, you reduce or limit it.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.ex: He runs with great vigour every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都充满精力地跑步。
words.en: Physical or mental strength and energy.

words.tr: n. 蠢人；笨人；呆子；白痴
words.ex: The oaf dropped his plate on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的人把盘子掉在了地上。
words.en: An oaf is a person who is clumsy, stupid, or uncultured.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；摇尾乞怜的
words.ex: He is fawning over the boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他正在讨好老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as fawning, you disapprove of it because it shows that they are trying too hard to please someone, often because they are eager for power or approval.

words.ex: The truculence of the opponent's team was evident in their aggressive play.
words.ex_cn: 对手球队的好战性在他们激烈的比赛中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being eager or quick to argue, fight, or start a conflict; aggressiveness.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.ex: He works hard to earn his subsistence.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以维持生计。
words.en: Subsistence is the condition of just having enough food or money to stay alive.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.tr: adj. 胆汁的；患胆病的；脾气暴躁的；恶心头痛的；让人恶心的
words.ex: He had a bilious complexion due to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于生病，他的脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is bilious, they are bad-tempered or irritable, often because of a problem with their liver or digestion.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.tr:
v. 品味；细品；享用；体会
n. 风味；滋味
words.ex: He savord the taste of the chocolate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地品味着巧克力的味道。
words.en: To enjoy or appreciate (something) completely.

words.tr:
n. 远足；短途旅游
v. 远足；短途旅游
words.ex: We decided to take a jaunt to the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定去乡间远足。
words.en: A short journey or excursion, especially one taken for pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 恰当的；贴切的；关系密切的
words.ex: His comment was germane to the topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论与话题恰当相关。
words.en: Something that is germane to a situation or idea is connected with it in an important way.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；不是时候的
words.ex: He called at an inopportune time.
words.ex_cn: 他在不恰当的时候打了电话。
words.en: If you describe something as inopportune, you mean that it happens at an unfortunate or unsuitable time, and causes trouble or embarrassment because of this.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: His face turned ashen after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的脸变得苍白。
words.en: If someone is ashen, their face is very pale, often because they are ill, shocked, or frightened.

words.ex: He showed his passport at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场出示了他的护照。
words.en: A passport is an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country and gives you the right to travel to and from that country.

words.tr: n. 做手势；做示意动作
words.ex: His animated gesticulation made it clear he was very excited about the proposal.
words.ex_cn: 他激动的示意动作表明他对这个提议非常兴奋。
words.en: Gesticulation refers to the act of making gestures, especially while speaking, to emphasize or illustrate what is being said.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.ex: He can discriminating between real and fake coins.
words.ex_cn: 他能区分真币和假币。
words.en: If you describe someone as discriminating, you mean that they are able to recognize and appreciate the good qualities of something, especially things that are of high quality.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.ex: The aggressor attacked the small village.
words.ex_cn: 侵略者袭击了那个小村庄。
words.en: An aggressor is a person, group, or country that starts a fight or war by attacking first.

words.ex: The war caused many atrocities.
words.ex_cn: 战争造成了许多暴行。
words.en: An atrocity is a very cruel, shocking, and morally unacceptable act.

words.ex: He is a horticultural expert who grows vegetables in his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位园艺专家，在自己的花园里种植蔬菜。
words.en: Relating to the art or practice of garden cultivation and management.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；爱吵架的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: The cantankerous old man yells at his neighbors every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位脾气暴躁的老人每天早上都对邻居大喊大叫。
words.en: Someone who is cantankerous is bad-tempered and quarrels with people.

words.ex: He has a culinary degree from a famous school.
words.ex_cn: 他从一所著名学校获得了烹饪学位。
words.en: Relating to cooking or the kitchen.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr: v. 使变白；（脸色）变苍白；焯
words.ex: She blanches the vegetables before freezing them.
words.ex_cn: 她在冷冻蔬菜之前先焯水。
words.en: To blanch means to make something white or pale, often by removing color or by causing it to lose color. It can also refer to the process of briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into cold water to halt the cooking process.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.tr: adj. 没有回报的；无报酬的；有仇未报的；单方面的
words.ex: She suffered from unrequited love for many years.
words.ex_cn: 多年来，她一直承受着单恋之苦。
words.en: If you say that something such as love or affection is unrequited, you mean that it is not returned by the person it is directed towards.

words.tr: v. 回报；报答；往复；来回
words.ex: She helped me, and I will reciprocate.
words.ex_cn: 她帮了我，我会回报她。
words.en: If your feelings or actions towards someone are reciprocated, the other person feels or behaves in the same way towards you as you have felt or behaved towards them.

words.ex: The two kids stayed in equilibrium on the seesaw.
words.ex_cn: 两个孩子在跷跷板上保持了平衡。
words.en: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.tr: adj. 放纵的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: His intemperate lifestyle led to numerous health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他放纵的生活方式导致了许多健康问题。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or behaviour as intemperate, you are critical of them because they are too extreme and uncontrolled.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.ex: The children laughed with jollity at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上欢快地笑着。
words.en: Jollity is the quality of being cheerful and having fun.

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的
n. 润肤剂；软化剂
words.ex: The cream is an emollient for dry skin.
words.ex_cn: 这种乳霜是用于干皮肤的润肤剂。
words.en: An emollient is a substance that softens or soothes the skin, or a statement or action that calms or reduces tension.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.ex: The movie has a thematic focus on friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的主题聚焦于友谊。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a theme or themes.

words.tr: adj. 有条纹的；有条痕的
words.ex: The rock had a striated surface, showing layers of different minerals.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石的表面有条纹，显示了不同矿物的层理。
words.en: Marked with striae; striped or grooved.

words.tr:
adj. 打乱的；混乱的； 扰乱的
v. 使混乱； 扰乱；“discombobulate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt discombobulated after losing her keys.
words.ex_cn: 她丢了钥匙后感到非常困惑。
words.en: If you are discombobulated, you are confused and cannot think clearly, often because you have been surprised or upset by something.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁辱骂的；恶语毁谤的；下流粗俗的
words.ex: The politician was criticized for making scurrilous remarks about his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客因对对手发表下流的言论而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something as scurrilous, you mean that it is vulgar and intended to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可挽救的；可矫正的
words.ex: The damage to the environment is remediable if we act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们迅速采取行动，对环境的破坏是可以补救的。
words.en: If something is remediable, it can be corrected or cured.

words.ex: The climactic scene of the movie surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 电影的高潮场景让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Relating to the most intense, exciting, or important point of something; reaching a climax.

words.tr: adj. 保险统计师的；保险精算的
words.ex: He is learning actuarial science to work in insurance.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习精算科学，以便从事保险工作。
words.en: Actuarial work involves the use of statistical methods to assess risk in insurance and finance industries.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

words.ex: They called him 'Quick Feet' as an epithet.
words.ex_cn: 他们用‘快脚’作为他的绰号。
words.en: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase added to or substituted for a person's name, often to describe a characteristic or quality.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr: adj. 记性好的；有保持力的
words.ex: She has a very retentive memory.
words.ex_cn: 她有非常好的记忆力。
words.en: If you have a retentive memory, you are able to remember things easily.

words.tr: v. 痛击；痛斥；冗长地解释
words.ex: He belabored the point until everyone was bored.
words.ex_cn: 他反复讨论那个观点，直到大家都感到厌烦。
words.en: To argue or discuss (a subject) in excessive detail; to attack or criticize (someone) persistently.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: The termination of the contract surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 合同的终止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of ending something or the end of something.

words.ex: His pugnacity made him argue with everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的好斗性格让他和每个人争论。
words.en: Pugnacity is the quality of being eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight.

words.ex: His domicile is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所位于纽约。
words.en: A domicile is the place where a person lives or has their home.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.ex: The exodus of people from the city happened after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，大批人离开了这座城市。
words.en: An exodus is a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time.

words.ex: The car's velocity increased on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在高速公路上的速度增加了。
words.en: Velocity is the speed at which something moves in a particular direction.

words.ex: He made an impious joke about the sacred temple.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣的寺庙开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as impious, you mean that they show a lack of respect for religious practices or beliefs.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.tr: n. （15–17世纪使用的）西班牙大帆船
words.ex: The galleon was a symbol of Spain's maritime power.
words.ex_cn: 这艘大型帆船是西班牙海上力量的象征。
words.en: A galleon is a large sailing ship with three or more masts, used especially by the Spanish for war and commerce during the 15th to 17th centuries.

words.ex: The company showed its largess by donating to several charities.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过向几家慈善机构捐款展示了它的慷慨。
words.en: Largess refers to the generous giving of gifts or money, often by a person of high status, such as a king or noble, to their subjects or followers.

words.tr: n. 小配角；小品文；浮雕宝石
words.ex: She appeared in a cameo role in the film.
words.ex_cn: 她在电影中扮演了一个配角。
words.en: A cameo is a small but noticeable part in a film or play, often played by a famous actor or actress. It can also refer to a piece of jewelry consisting of a raised design on a background of a different color.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.ex: The rocket uses solid propellants to fly.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用固体推进剂飞行。
words.en: Propellants are substances used to propel something, especially in the context of rockets and firearms, where they provide the necessary force for lift-off or firing.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.tr: n. 眼镜商；验光师；眼镜商店
words.ex: He visited the optician to get new glasses.
words.ex_cn: 他去眼镜店配了新眼镜。
words.en: A person who makes or sells eyeglasses and other optical instruments.

words.tr: n. 国家或组织的法定歌曲
words.ex: The team sang the national anthem before the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛前，球队唱了国歌。
words.en: An anthem is a song that is used to represent a particular nation, society, or group and that is sung on special occasions.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.tr:
n. 重复部分；再现
v. 重演；重奏
words.ex: The song ended with a short reprise of the chorus.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌以副歌的简短重复部分结束。
words.en: A reprise is a repetition of a piece of music or a performance. It can also refer to the act of repeating something.

words.tr: n. 无稽之谈；胡言乱语
words.ex: He spoke gibberish, making it impossible to understand his message.
words.ex_cn: 他语无伦次，让人无法理解他的意思。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or ideas as gibberish, you mean that they do not make any sense.

words.tr: n. 巨头；大亨；大资本家
words.ex: The magnate owns many hotels and airlines.
words.ex_cn: 这位大亨拥有许多酒店和航空公司。
words.en: A magnate is a person who is very rich and powerful, especially in a particular industry.

words.tr:
adj. 甜得发腻的；令人腻烦的
v. 感到腻烦；“cloy”的现在分词
words.ex: The cloying sweetness of the cake made me sick.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕过于甜腻的味道让我感到恶心。
words.en: If you describe something as cloying, you mean that it is so sweet or sentimental that it is unpleasant.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.tr:
adj. 认命的；顺从的；勉强接受的
v. 辞职；“resign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was resigned to losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他认命地接受了输掉比赛的结果。
words.en: If you are resigned to an unpleasant situation or fact, you accept it without complaining because you realize that you cannot change it.

words.ex: His timidity made him afraid to speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 他的胆怯让他不敢在课堂上发言。
words.en: The quality or state of being timid; lack of courage or self-confidence.

words.tr: adj. 心烦意乱的；忧心如焚的
words.ex: She was distraught when she lost her dog.
words.ex_cn: 当她丢失了她的狗时，她非常悲痛。
words.en: If someone is distraught, they are so upset and worried that they cannot think clearly.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: adj. 非实体的；非物质的；无形体的
words.ex: The ghost is incorporeal and cannot be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这个幽灵是无形的，无法被触碰。
words.en: Not composed of matter; having no material existence.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.ex: The blood began to congeal on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 血液开始在地面上凝结。
words.en: If a liquid congeals, it becomes very thick and sticky and almost solid.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.tr: n. 挽歌；哀歌；忧伤的歌
words.ex: They sang a slow dirge at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他们在葬礼上唱了一首缓慢的哀歌。
words.en: A dirge is a slow, sad song or piece of music, sometimes played at a funeral.

words.ex: The party was a fiasco because no one came.
words.ex_cn: 派对是一场灾难，因为没人来。
words.en: A fiasco is something that is a complete failure, especially in a way that is very embarrassing or disappointing.

words.ex: The solemnity of the ceremony made everyone quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式的庄重让所有人都安静了下来。
words.en: The state or quality of being serious and dignified.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: n. （术语）纵火狂患者；（非正式）爱玩火（或看火）的人
words.ex: He is a pyromaniac who loves setting fires.
words.ex_cn: 他是个纵火狂，喜欢放火。
words.en: A pyromaniac is a person who has an uncontrollable desire to set fire to things.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: The finale of the concert was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会的终曲非常激动人心。
words.en: The finale is the last part of a piece of music, a performance, or a public event, especially when this is particularly dramatic or exciting.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: His peregrinations through Europe were filled with adventure and discovery.
words.ex_cn: 他在欧洲的游历充满了冒险和发现。
words.en: A long journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.tr: adj. 造成创伤的；痛苦的；不愉快的
words.ex: The car accident was a traumatic experience.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次创伤性的经历。
words.en: If something is traumatic, it causes you severe emotional distress and anxiety.

words.ex: She poured the pasta through a colander.
words.ex_cn: 她把意大利面倒进漏勺里。
words.en: A colander is a bowl-shaped kitchen utensil with holes in it used for draining food such as pasta or washing vegetables.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: He wrote the book for posterity.
words.ex_cn: 他写这本书是为了留给后人。
words.en: All future generations of people.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.tr: adj. 不能补救的；不能挽回的
words.ex: The damage to the painting was irremediable.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的损坏是无法挽回的。
words.en: If something is irremediable, it is impossible to correct or improve.

words.ex: The movie had prurient scenes that upset many viewers.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有令人不适的色情场面。
words.en: Having or encouraging an excessive interest in sexual matters.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.ex: He writes his name in cursive.
words.ex_cn: 他用草书写自己的名字。
words.en: Cursive is a style of handwriting in which the letters are joined together in a flowing manner.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: The movie was banned for its lewd content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因内容猥亵而被禁播。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as lewd, you are critical of it because it is sexual in a rude and unpleasant way.

words.ex: He is an ornithologist who watches birds every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名鸟类学家，每天观察鸟类。
words.en: An ornithologist is a person who studies or is an expert in ornithology, the branch of zoology that deals with the study of birds.

words.tr:
adj. 咸的；辛辣的；好吃的；好闻的
n. 咸味小吃
words.ex: The savory snack made her thirsty.
words.ex_cn: 这道咸味小吃让她口渴了。
words.en: Savory food is pleasantly salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.tr: v. 吐；“spit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The cat spat out the pill.
words.ex_cn: 猫把药丸吐了出来。
words.en: A spat is a short, usually minor, argument or disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 自我本位的；任性的；自负的
words.ex: He is egotistical and always talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自我中心，总是谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egotistical, you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are more important or better than other people.

words.tr:
v. 争论；讲价
n. 讨价还价；争论
words.ex: They haggle over the price of the car.
words.ex_cn: 他们为汽车的价格争论。
words.en: If you haggle, you argue about something, especially about the price of something you want to buy.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.tr:
v. 散发臭气；发出难闻的气味；洋溢；充满
n. 恶臭；难闻的气味
words.ex: The garbage reeks in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾在烈日下散发恶臭。
words.en: To reek of something means to smell very strongly of it, especially in an unpleasant way.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: The farmer used a drone to check his crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民用无人驾驶飞机检查他的庄稼。
words.en: A drone is a male bee that does not work and exists solely to mate with the queen bee. It can also refer to an unmanned aircraft or ship guided by remote control or onboard computers. Additionally, 'drone' can describe a continuous low humming sound or to speak in a monotonous tone.

words.ex: The teacher will stratify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师会按年龄将学生分层。
words.en: To arrange or form into layers or strata.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The eagle gripped the rabbit with its talon.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰用它的爪子抓住了兔子。
words.en: The claw of a bird of prey.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.ex: Vegetables are rich in nutrient.
words.ex_cn: 蔬菜富含营养物。
words.en: A nutrient is a substance that is essential for life and growth, such as the vitamins and minerals in food.

words.ex: The project began at its inception.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目从开始时就启动了。
words.en: The inception of something is the start or beginning of it.

words.ex: The cession of land was agreed upon by both countries.
words.ex_cn: 两国同意转让土地。
words.en: The act of ceding or giving up something, especially land or rights, to another party.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.ex: She is a coquette who flirts with everyone.
words.ex_cn: 她是个对每个人都卖弄风情的女子。
words.en: A coquette is a woman who flirts lightheartedly with men to win their admiration and affection.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 高兴得咯咯笑；哈哈大笑
n. 哈哈大笑；开心地笑
words.ex: He chortled when he saw the funny cat.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的猫时咯咯笑了。
words.en: To laugh in a breathy, gleeful way; chuckle.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.ex: He is a pragmatist who solves problems with real solutions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个注重实际解决方案的实用主义者。
words.en: A pragmatist is someone who is pragmatic, that is, someone who is practical and focused on reaching a goal. Pragmatists are results-oriented and often have a no-nonsense approach to solving problems.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.tr:
n. 睡眠；
v. 睡觉；
words.ex: He needs more sleep to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他需要更多的睡眠来感觉好些。
words.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind is unconscious.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.tr:
adj. 易燃的；燃烧性的；易激动的
n. 燃质物；可燃物
words.ex: The wood is combustible and burns easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种木头是可燃的，容易燃烧。
words.en: A combustible material or gas catches fire and burns easily.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: The plan went awry when the rain started.
words.ex_cn: 当雨下起来时，计划就出差错了。
words.en: If something goes awry, it does not happen in the way that was planned.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: The culvert under the road was designed to handle heavy rainwater flow.
words.ex_cn: 道路下的涵洞设计用于处理大雨的排水。
words.en: A culvert is a tunnel carrying a stream or open drain under a road or railway.

words.ex: He stood on the podium to receive the gold medal.
words.ex_cn: 他站在领奖台上领取金牌。
words.en: A podium is a small platform on which someone stands to give a speech or conduct an orchestra, or on which a medal winner stands during a prize-giving ceremony.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.tr: adj. 大量地给予的；不吝啬的
words.ex: She was unstinting in her praise for the volunteers.
words.ex_cn: 她对志愿者们给予了慷慨的赞扬。
words.en: If you describe someone's support or effort as unstinting, you mean that they give it generously and completely, without holding back.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；狂热的；疯狂的
words.ex: He had a maniacal glint in his eyes as he spoke about his new project.
words.ex_cn: 他谈起自己的新项目时，眼中闪烁着狂热的光芒。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as maniacal, you mean that it is extremely wild and often violent because they are mentally ill or very angry.

words.ex: He checked the glossary for the meaning of new words.
words.ex_cn: 他查阅了术语表以了解新词的含义。
words.en: A glossary is a list of terms in a particular domain of knowledge with the definitions for those terms.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.tr:
v. 大步走；大步跑
n. 大步慢跑；平稳、轻松的步伐
words.ex: The deer loped gracefully through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 鹿优雅地大步慢跑穿过森林。
words.en: To run or move with a long, easy stride.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr:
n. 混乱；一团糟
v. 蹒跚地走；踉跄而行；“shamble”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The room was a complete shambles after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对过后，房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A state of total disorder.

words.ex: The two companies were accused of collusion to fix prices.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司被指控串通操纵价格。
words.en: Collusion is secret or illegal cooperation or conspiracy, especially in order to cheat or deceive others.

words.ex: Bees and flowers have symbiosis.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂和花朵之间有共生关系。
words.en: Symbiosis is a close relationship between two different kinds of living things in which each provides something that the other needs.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.ex: She is weaning her baby off milk.
words.ex_cn: 她正在让宝宝戒掉牛奶。
words.en: To wean someone off something means to make them gradually stop using or depending on it, especially something harmful or unnecessary.

words.tr: n. 警戒线；绶带；束带层; vt. 用警戒线围住；包围隔离; n. （Cordon）人名；（英、西...
words.ex: Police cordoned off the area after the explosion.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸发生后，警察用警戒线封锁了该区域。
words.en: A cordon is a line of police, soldiers, or vehicles that is positioned around an area to prevent people from entering or leaving it.

words.ex: He felt vertigo after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕。
words.en: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, associated particularly with looking down from a great height, or caused by disease affecting the inner ear or the vestibular nerve; giddiness.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.tr:
adj. 波动的；起伏的
v. 使波动；使起伏；“undulate”的现在分词
words.ex: The road is undulating through the hills.
words.ex_cn: 这条路在山丘间起伏蜿蜒。
words.en: Moving with a smooth wavelike motion.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.tr: adj. 无道德观念的；不辨是非的
words.ex: He made an amoral decision to lie for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱做出了一个不道德的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as amoral, you mean that they do not consider whether their behavior is morally right or wrong.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.ex: He showed forbearance when his friend made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友犯错时，他表现出了忍耐。
words.en: Forbearance is the quality of being patient and being able to control your temper in difficult situations.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.ex: The piebald horse trotted gracefully across the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 那匹花斑马优雅地小跑穿过草地。
words.en: A piebald animal has patches of black and white on it.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: The old adage says, 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 这句古老的格言说：'慢而稳者胜。'
words.en: An adage is a short, wise saying which has been used for a long time and is generally accepted as true.

words.ex: He gave a quick rejoinder to her question.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的问题迅速做出了回应。
words.en: A rejoinder is a reply, especially a quick or witty one, to a question or remark.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: The company hired an expert to do an audit.
words.ex_cn: 公司聘请了一位专家进行审计。
words.en: An audit is an official examination of the accounts of a business or organization to check that they are accurate and correct.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: n. 飞地；被包围的领土
words.ex: The village is an enclave surrounded by forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄是一个被森林包围的飞地。
words.en: An enclave is a part of a country or a group of people that is surrounded by another country or group of people.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.tr:
v. 窃笑；嗤嗤地笑；傻笑
n. 短促而神经质的笑
words.ex: She couldn't help but titter at the ridiculous situation.
words.ex_cn: 她忍不住对这个荒谬的情况窃笑。
words.en: To laugh in a restrained, self-conscious, or nervous way.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: Clean water is a boon to the village.
words.ex_cn: 干净的水对这个村庄是有益的。
words.en: A boon is something that is very helpful and improves the quality of life.

words.ex: The old building was in a state of decrepitude.
words.ex_cn: 这座老建筑处于一种破败的状态。
words.en: Decrepitude refers to the state of being old and in poor condition, especially as a result of age or long use.

words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.ex: The sect held unusual beliefs that differed from the main religion.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别的信仰与主流宗教不同。
words.en: A sect is a group of people who have different religious beliefs from other people in the same religion.

words.ex: The judge criticized the lawyer for his prolixity in the court.
words.ex_cn: 法官批评了律师在法庭上的冗长发言。
words.en: Prolixity refers to the use of too many words to express an idea, making speech or writing tediously lengthy.

words.ex: The luxuriant forest had thick trees and deep green leaves.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林有茂盛的树木和深绿色的叶子。
words.en: Luxuriant is used to describe something that is rich in growth, abundance, or opulence.

words.ex: The boundless sky made her feel free.
words.ex_cn: 无边无际的天空让她感到自由。
words.en: If you describe something as boundless, you mean that it has no limits or seems to be without limits.

words.ex: His actions were marked by turpitude and deceit.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为充满了卑鄙和欺骗。
words.en: Turpitude refers to depravity or wickedness, especially in a moral sense.

words.ex: The storm sundered the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树劈开了。
words.en: To break or split apart, especially along a natural line or grain.

words.tr: n. 大数目；多种多样；繁多
words.ex: There is a multiplicity of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有大量星星。
words.en: A multiplicity of things or people means a large number or great variety of them.

words.ex: The two notes sound consonance together.
words.ex_cn: 这两个音一起听起来很和谐。
words.en: Consonance refers to agreement or harmony between things or people, or the repetition of consonant sounds in poetry or music.

words.ex: She felt revulsion when she saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到那脏兮兮的食物时，感到非常厌恶。
