words.en: A sudden and intense feeling of disgust or loathing.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.ex: The sky is illimitable.
words.ex_cn: 天空是无边无际的。
words.en: If you describe something as illimitable, you mean that it is extremely large or great in degree or extent.

words.ex: The country agreed to extradition of the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 该国同意引渡这名嫌疑人。
words.en: The act of officially sending someone back to their own country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of in another country.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.tr: n. 剧本；歌词；歌剧脚本
words.ex: He wrote the libretto for a famous opera.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部著名的歌剧写了剧本。
words.en: The text of an opera or other long vocal work.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.ex: The loan requires collateral documents.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款需要附属文件。
words.en: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.ex: The rain stymied our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了我们去远足的计划。
words.en: To stymie someone or something means to prevent them from achieving their aims.

words.ex: The linchpin holds the wheel in place.
words.ex_cn: 制轮楔将车轮固定到位。
words.en: A linchpin is a person or thing that is essential to the success or operation of something.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.ex: The crime scene was grisly and made everyone feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 犯罪现场很可怕，让所有人都感到恶心。
words.en: Grisly is used to describe something that is extremely unpleasant and horrifying, often because it involves death or violence.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.ex: The party was filled with revelry and laughter.
words.ex_cn: 派对上充满了狂欢和笑声。
words.en: Revelry is a situation in which people are enjoying themselves in a lively and noisy way, often while they are drinking alcohol.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: The project is in abeyance until next year.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目暂时搁置，直到明年。
words.en: A state of temporary disuse or suspension.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.ex: He used too much verbiage in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他在邮件中用了太多的冗词。
words.en: Verbiage refers to an overabundance of words in writing or speech, often seen as unnecessary or overly complex.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.tr: adj. 不善交际的；不圆滑的；笨拙的
words.ex: He made a gauche comment at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上说了个笨拙的评论。
words.en: If you describe someone as gauche, you mean that they are awkward and uncomfortable in the company of other people, especially because they lack social skills.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.ex: The lambs gambol in the green field.
words.ex_cn: 小羊在绿地上嬉戏。
words.en: If animals or people gambol, they run or jump about in a playful way.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.ex: He is my confidant and I tell him everything.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的知己，我什么都告诉他。
words.en: A confidant is someone you can share your secrets with or discuss personal matters with, knowing that they will keep your information private.

words.tr:
adj. 据称的；传言的
v. 声称；意指；意味着；“purport”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The purported owner of the car was not the real one.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的所谓主人并不是真正的主人。
words.en: If you say that something purports to be true or to have a particular quality, you mean that it claims to be true or to have that quality, although it may not be.

words.ex: The team's loss was a total debacle.
words.ex_cn: 球队的失败是一场彻底的惨败。
words.en: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or collapse, often in a way that is very embarrassing or causes a lot of damage.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.ex: He is learning alchemy from an old book.
words.ex_cn: 他正从一本旧书中学习炼金术。
words.en: Alchemy is an ancient practice that aimed to transform base metals into gold and to discover a universal cure for disease and a way of extending life.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；共振的；引起共鸣的；
words.ex: The bell has a resonant sound.
words.ex_cn: 这口钟的声音洪亮。
words.en: A sound that is resonant is deep, strong, and clear, often because it is produced in a space that echoes or amplifies it.

words.tr:
n. 硬币；金属钱币；
v. 创造；
words.ex: He has a coin in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他口袋里有一枚硬币。
words.en: A coin is a small, flat, round piece of metal or plastic that is used as money.

words.tr: adj. 时代错误的；落伍的；过时的
words.ex: Wearing a horse-drawn carriage in modern times is anachronistic.
words.ex_cn: 在现代穿马车是过时的。
words.en: Something that is anachronistic is out of its proper time in history, or seems to belong to a different time.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: He got compensatory pay for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了补偿性工资。
words.en: Compensatory is used to describe something that is intended to compensate for something else, especially loss or damage.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.ex: The teacher helps students demystify math problems.
words.ex_cn: 老师帮助学生弄明白数学问题。
words.en: To make something easier to understand by explaining it in a clear and simple way.

words.tr:
adj. 酒醉的；陶醉的
v. 使醉；使陶醉；“inebriate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was inebriated after a night of heavy drinking.
words.ex_cn: 经过一夜的酗酒，他醉了。
words.en: If someone is inebriated, they have drunk too much alcohol and are drunk.

words.tr:
n. 泥潭；泥沼；困境
v. 使陷进泥坑里
words.ex: The car got stuck in the mire.
words.ex_cn: 汽车陷在泥沼里了。
words.en: Mire refers to an area of wet, soggy ground or a difficult situation from which it is hard to extricate oneself.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.tr: n. 鼎盛时期；（人生或事业的)巅峰；册封为神
words.ex: The artist's work reached apotheosis in his final masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品在他的最终杰作中达到了神化。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; culmination or climax.

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.tr: n. 口技表演者；腹语表演者；
words.ex: The ventriloquist made his doll talk funny.
words.ex_cn: 这位口技表演者让他的玩偶说起了滑稽的话。
words.en: A ventriloquist is someone who can speak without moving their lips and who entertains people by making it seem as if a puppet is talking.

words.ex: The evidence helps to exculpate him.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据有助于为他开脱。
words.en: To remove blame from someone; to declare or prove someone not guilty of wrongdoing.

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.ex: The police caught the malefactor who stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓到了偷钱的罪犯。
words.en: A malefactor is someone who has committed a crime or done something wrong.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.ex: He doffed his hat as a sign of respect.
words.ex_cn: 他脱帽以示敬意。
words.en: To remove an item of clothing, especially a hat.

words.tr: n. 叛教者；脱党者；变节者
words.ex: He became an apostate after leaving the church.
words.ex_cn: 他离开教会后成了叛教者。
words.en: An apostate is someone who has abandoned their religious faith, political loyalties, or principles.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.ex: He is the beneficiary of his father's will.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父亲遗嘱的受益人。
words.en: A beneficiary is someone who receives money or other benefits as a result of something, especially a will or insurance policy.

words.ex: He feels dizzy because of his acrophobia when he looks down from the tall building.
words.ex_cn: 他从高楼往下看时因为恐高而感到头晕。
words.en: An extreme or irrational fear of heights.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr: adj. 憔悴的；形容枯槁的
words.ex: He looked haggard after working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他熬了一整夜后看起来憔悴不堪。
words.en: Someone who is haggard looks exhausted and unwell, often because they have been through a very difficult or stressful experience.

words.ex: The auditory system helps us hear sounds.
words.ex_cn: 听觉系统帮助我们听到声音。
words.en: Relating to the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.ex: The owl's appearance was seen as an augury of bad luck.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰的出现被视为厄运的预兆。
words.en: An augury is a sign of what will happen in the future, often based on the interpretation of omens or the behavior of birds.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: The pollution caused the degradation of the river.
words.ex_cn: 污染导致了河流的恶化。
words.en: The process by which something is reduced in quality, value, or status.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: They made a concerted effort to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同努力清理了公园。
words.en: A concerted action or effort is done by several people or groups working together.

words.ex: He used guile to trick the guard.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计骗过了守卫。
words.en: Guile is the quality of being skilled at deceiving people in order to achieve something.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.ex: The country has an agrarian economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个农业经济。
words.en: Relating to land, especially agricultural land, or to the ownership or division of such land.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 猥亵的；淫秽的；诲淫的；好色的
words.ex: The novel was criticized for its salacious content.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说因其淫秽内容而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book or joke as salacious, you think that it deals with sexual matters in an unnecessarily detailed way.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.tr: n. 技巧；敏捷手法；策略；戏法
words.ex: The magician used sleight to make the coin disappear.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师用技巧让硬币消失了。
words.en: Skill in using the hands, especially in performing tricks.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.tr: n. 导管；管道；水管；水道
words.ex: The cable is a conduit for electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这根电缆是电的通道。
words.en: A conduit is a channel or pipe for conveying water or other fluid.

words.ex: The rider rode his horse quickly across the field.
words.ex_cn: 骑手快速骑马穿过田野。
words.en: A rider is someone who rides a horse, bicycle, or motorcycle, or a clause added to a document that provides additional information or conditions.

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.tr: n. 初进社交界的少女
words.ex: The debutante's ball was a grand affair attended by the elite of society.
words.ex_cn: 这位初次进入社交界的年轻女子的舞会是一场盛大的活动，社会精英纷纷出席。
words.en: A debutante is a young woman from a wealthy or upper-class family who is making her first formal appearance in society, typically at a debutante ball.

words.tr: n. 装模作样的人；装腔作势的人
words.ex: He was always seen as a poseur, trying too hard to fit in with the cool crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他总是被视为一个装模作样的人，过于努力地想融入酷酷的群体。
words.en: A poseur is someone who behaves in an artificial way in order to impress other people.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.ex: He had a misapprehension about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则有一个误解。
words.en: A misapprehension is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to a mistaken belief or idea.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

words.ex: He swore a vendetta against his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他向邻居发誓要报仇。
words.en: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel with or campaign against someone.

words.ex: His arrogance made others dislike him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人不喜欢他。
words.en: Arrogance is the quality of being arrogant, which means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；敏捷的；充满生气的
words.ex: The old man is still spry and walks fast.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人仍然身手敏捷，走得很慢。
words.en: Someone who is spry, especially an older person, is lively and active.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: The teacher gave an unintimidating smile.
words.ex_cn: 老师露出了一个令人安心的微笑。
words.en: Not causing fear or a feeling of being threatened; approachable.

words.ex: She is a comely girl with a sweet smile.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个面容姣好、带着甜美微笑的姑娘。
words.en: Pleasant to look at; attractive.

words.tr: adj. 恶臭的；有恶臭的；有臭味的
words.ex: The malodorous garbage was attracting flies.
words.ex_cn: 那堆有恶臭的垃圾招来了苍蝇。
words.en: Having a very unpleasant smell.

words.tr: adj. 斜躺的；斜靠的；侧卧的
words.ex: The old man sat in a recumbent chair.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人坐在一张躺椅上。
words.en: A recumbent position or posture is one in which a person is lying down or leaning back in a relaxed manner.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: The merger of two companies created a bigger business.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司的合并创建了一家更大的企业。
words.en: A merger is the joining together of two separate companies or organizations so that they become one.

words.tr: n. 模仿作品；风格拼凑的艺术作品
words.ex: The movie is a pastiche of various genres.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是各种类型的混成曲。
words.en: A pastiche is a work of art, literature, or music that imitates the style of someone else's work or is a mixture of different styles.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.tr: n. 大片土地；体内管道；
words.ex: The farmer owns a large tract of land near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有靠近河边的一大片土地。
words.en: A tract is a large area of land or a system of connected organs in the body.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: The man was incarcerated for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: If people are incarcerated, they are kept in a prison or other place.

words.tr: n. 巨兽；庞然大物；巨头
words.ex: The company is a behemoth in the tech industry.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是科技行业中的巨无霸。
words.en: A behemoth is something that is extremely large and powerful, often referring to an organization, project, or thing that is so large it is difficult to manage or control.

words.ex: We had dinner at a buffet with many dishes to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 我们在自助餐吃了晚饭，有很多菜可以选。
words.en: A buffet is a meal consisting of several dishes from which guests serve themselves. As a verb, to buffet means to strike repeatedly and violently.

words.tr: adj. 著名的； v. 庆祝；“celebrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a celebrated painter in China.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在中国著名的画家。
words.en: A celebrated person or thing is famous and much admired.

words.ex: He signed an indenture to work for five years.
words.ex_cn: 他签署了一份契约，同意工作五年。
words.en: An indenture is a formal legal agreement, contract, or document, such as a bond or a deed, especially one that specifies the terms of a debt or obligation.

words.tr:
n. 失败主义者
adj. 失败主义的
words.ex: The defeatist attitude of the team was quickly noticed by the coach.
words.ex_cn: 教练很快就注意到了队伍中失败主义的态度。
words.en: A defeatist is someone who gives up too easily or accepts defeat without trying hard enough to prevent it.

words.ex: The plants grow in the conservatory.
words.ex_cn: 植物在温室里生长。
words.en: A conservatory is a room with glass walls and a glass roof, which is built on the side of a house. It is used as a sun lounge or for growing plants. It can also refer to a school where people are trained in music or acting.

words.tr: adj. 态度暧昧的；不表态的；含糊的
words.ex: He gave a noncommittal answer when asked about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到计划时，他给出了一个模棱两可的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or attitude as noncommittal, you mean that they do not express their opinion or intentions clearly.

words.tr: adj. 臭名远扬的；声名狼藉的；
words.ex: He is an infamous thief who stole from many banks.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个臭名远扬的窃贼，偷过许多银行。
words.en: If you say that someone is infamous, you mean that they are well known because they have done something bad.

words.ex: He is a celibate priest who never married.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位从未结婚的独身神父。
words.en: Someone who is celibate does not marry or have sex, often because of religious beliefs.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.ex: He made a gaffe when he called the boss by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老板的名字，犯了个错误。
words.en: A gaffe is a mistake that a person makes in public, especially something embarrassing that they say or do.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.ex: He cozens his friend into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他哄骗朋友借给他钱。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr: n. 语文学；语言学；文献学
words.ex: He loves philology because it helps him understand old texts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱语言学，因为它帮助他理解古文。
words.en: Philology is the study of language in written historical sources; it is a combination of literary studies, history and linguistics.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.tr: adj. 感情脆弱的；易落泪的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She was feeling maudlin after watching the sentimental movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完那部感人的电影后，她感到非常伤感。
words.en: If you describe someone as maudlin, you mean that they are being sad and sentimental in a foolish way, perhaps because of drinking alcohol.

words.tr: n. 补药；滋补品；奎宁水
words.ex: He drank a tonic to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一杯滋补剂来感觉好些。
words.en: A tonic is a medicine that makes you feel stronger, healthier, and less tired.

words.ex: He eats gourmet food at a fancy restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家高档餐厅吃精致美食。
words.en: A gourmet is someone who knows a lot about food and cooking, and who enjoys eating high-quality food.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的；专心致志的
words.ex: The children were rapt during the story.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们全神贯注地听故事。
words.en: If someone is rapt, they are so interested in or fascinated by what they are seeing or hearing that they do not pay attention to anything else.

words.ex: He had a misconception that the earth is flat.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个错误认识，认为地球是平的。
words.en: A misconception is an idea that is not correct because it is based on a misunderstanding or a wrong belief.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.tr: n. 扫兴的人；煞风景的人
words.ex: She was a killjoy, always finding something to complain about.
words.ex_cn: 她是个令人扫兴的人，总是能找到抱怨的事情。
words.en: A killjoy is someone who spoils other people's fun or enjoyment.

words.tr:
v. 严重伤害；粗暴对待；抨击
n. 大木槌
words.ex: The bear mauled the hiker, leaving deep wounds.
words.ex_cn: 熊袭击了徒步者，留下了深深的伤口。
words.en: To maul someone or something means to attack them and cause them serious injury, or to handle them roughly.

words.ex: He bought gold bullion as an investment.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了金条作为投资。
words.en: Gold or silver in bulk before coining, or valued by weight.

words.tr: n. 接触传染病；传染；歪风；蔓延
words.ex: The contagion spread quickly among the children.
words.ex_cn: 这种传染病在孩子们中迅速传播。
words.en: A contagion is the spreading of a disease, especially one that is caused by bacteria or viruses, from one person or animal to another by direct or indirect contact.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.tr: adj. 饮食的；营养的；与消化有关的
words.ex: The alimentary canal helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 消化道帮助消化食物。
words.en: Relating to nourishment or sustenance.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.ex: Kangaroos are marsupials that carry babies in a pouch.
words.ex_cn: 袋鼠是有袋动物，它们把幼崽放在育儿袋里。
words.en: A marsupial is a type of mammal that carries its young in a pouch.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔似的；残忍的；穷凶极恶的
words.ex: The plot of the movie was diabolical, filled with twists and turns.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节充满了曲折和转折，非常恶魔化。
words.en: If you describe something as diabolical, you are emphasizing that it is very bad, extreme, or unpleasant.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: Her insolence made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: Insolence is rude and disrespectful behavior.

words.tr:
v. 脱毛；换毛
n. 脱毛；换毛
words.ex: The bird molts its feathers every spring.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每年春天都会脱毛。
words.en: When an animal molts, it loses its feathers, hair, or skin so that new ones can grow.

words.tr:
adj. 沙文主义的；本着…第一主义者
n. 沙文主义者；盲目的爱国者
words.ex: He is a chauvinist who thinks men are better than women.
words.ex_cn: 他是个沙文主义者，认为男人比女人优秀。
words.en: A chauvinist is a person who believes in the superiority of their own group, especially their own gender or nationality, often to the point of being prejudiced against other groups.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.tr: n. 上行坡；向上的斜坡
words.ex: The path became steeper as they ascended the acclivity.
words.ex_cn: 随着他们攀登斜坡，道路变得更加陡峭。
words.en: An acclivity is a slope or piece of ground that slopes upward.

words.ex: The hulking man lifted the heavy box easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个魁梧的男人轻松地举起了沉重的箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as hulking, you mean that they are extremely large and often that they are also awkward or ugly.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: The teacher gave an encomium to the student for her perfect score.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生得了满分而给予了赞美。
words.en: A formal expression of praise; a eulogy.

words.ex: The gustatory sense helps us taste food.
words.ex_cn: 味觉帮助我们品尝食物。
words.en: Relating to the sense of taste.

words.ex: He is ambidextrous and can write with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他是左右手都灵巧的，可以用两只手写字。
words.en: Someone who is ambidextrous can use both their right and left hands equally well.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.ex: The car depreciates every year.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车每年都会贬值。
words.en: If something such as a currency depreciates or if something depreciates it, it loses some of its original value.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr:
adj. 毛发竖立的；浓密粗硬的；精神焕发的
v. 大为恼怒；耸起毛发；“bristle”的现在分词
words.ex: The cat was bristling with anger.
words.ex_cn: 那只猫因愤怒而毛发竖立。
words.en: If something is bristling with particular things, it has a lot of them or they are very noticeable.

words.ex: He was always the laggard in the race.
words.ex_cn: 在比赛中他总是落后者。
words.en: A laggard is someone who is very slow to do something or to make progress.

words.ex: The sun vaporizes water from the lake.
words.ex_cn: 太阳把湖里的水蒸发了。
words.en: To convert or be converted into vapor.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.tr: v. 盛情招待；尽情吃喝；使欢悦
words.ex: He regaled us with stories of his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他给我们讲了他旅行的故事，让我们很开心。
words.en: To regale someone means to entertain them with stories or to provide them with a lot of enjoyable food and drink.

words.ex: The forest has rich flora with many wild flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有丰富的植物，有许多野花。
words.en: The plants of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.

words.ex: The imputation of blame was unjust.
words.ex_cn: 归咎于责备是不公平的。
words.en: The act of imputing something, especially a fault or crime, to someone.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.ex: He loves ornithology and watches birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱鸟类学，每天早上都观察鸟类。
words.en: Ornithology is the branch of zoology that deals with the study of birds.

words.tr: n. 厚颜无耻；无礼；放肆
words.ex: His impudence surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的无礼让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impudence, you mean it is rude and disrespectful.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.tr:
n. 猛玛（象）；庞然大物；
adj. 巨大的；庞大的；
words.ex: The mammoth lived in cold areas long ago.
words.ex_cn: 猛犸象很久以前生活在寒冷地区。
words.en: If you describe something as mammoth, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large.

words.ex: The felon went to prison for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这名重罪犯因偷窃而入狱。
words.en: A felon is someone who is guilty of committing a felony, which is a serious crime such as murder or rape.

words.ex: The water freezes at zero centigrade.
words.ex_cn: 水在零摄氏度时结冰。
words.en: Centigrade is a scale for measuring temperature, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: The builder used a plumb to check if the wall was straight.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工人用铅锤检查墙是否垂直。
words.en: To measure the depth of water with a plumb line; to explore or understand something deeply; exactly vertical; completely or directly.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.tr: adj. 扭歪的；啼笑皆非的；挖苦的；讽刺的
words.ex: He gave a wry smile when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时露出了苦笑。
words.en: If someone has a wry expression, it shows that they find a bad situation or a change in a situation slightly amusing.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: My sibling plays soccer every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我的兄弟/姐妹每个周末都踢足球。
words.en: A sibling is a brother or sister.

words.ex: The responsiveness of the touchscreen is very good.
words.ex_cn: 这个触摸屏的敏感性很好。
words.en: The quality of reacting quickly and positively.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: He has a swarthy complexion from working outside.
words.ex_cn: 他因在户外工作而皮肤黝黑。
words.en: Having a dark complexion or skin color, especially as a result of exposure to the sun.

words.ex: The ancient hunter is the progenitor of our family.
words.ex_cn: 这位古代猎人是我们家族的祖先。
words.en: A progenitor is a direct ancestor of someone or the originator of a particular idea or movement.

words.tr: n. 省略号；省略；省略符号
words.ex: He used an ellipsis to show he stopped talking.
words.ex_cn: 他用了省略号来表示他停止了说话。
words.en: An ellipsis is a set of three dots (...) used in writing to indicate an omission of words or a pause.

words.ex: The smell of rotten food nauseates me.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味让我想吐。
words.en: If something nauseates you, it makes you feel as if you are going to vomit.

words.tr: n. 厌恶；嫌弃；排斥；斥力
words.ex: The sight filled her with repulsion.
words.ex_cn: 那景象让她感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of intense distaste or disgust.

words.tr: adj. 色情的； 多情的； 爱情的
words.ex: The movie showed amorous scenes that shocked the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了让观众震惊的色情场景。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as amorous, you mean that they involve sexual desire.

words.tr: adj. 不可剥夺（或分割）的
words.ex: Freedom is an inalienable right.
words.ex_cn: 自由是不可剥夺的权利。
words.en: An inalienable right or quality is one that cannot be taken away from you.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.tr: v. （在废物中）寻觅；食腐肉；拾荒
words.ex: Dogs scavenge for food in the streets.
words.ex_cn: 狗在街上翻找食物。
words.en: To scavenge means to search for and collect anything usable from discarded waste.

words.tr: adj. 幼芽的；胚种的；萌发的
words.ex: The germinal stage of an organism is crucial for its development.
words.ex_cn: 生物体的胚种阶段对其发育至关重要。
words.en: relating to or occurring in the earliest stage of development

words.tr: adj. 讲究礼仪的；隆重的
words.ex: He gave a ceremonious speech at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他在婚礼上发表了一篇庄重的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as ceremonious, you mean that they are very formal or polite.

words.tr: n. 大锅；动荡不安的局势
words.ex: The witch stirred the potion in her cauldron.
words.ex_cn: 女巫在她的锅里搅拌药水。
words.en: A cauldron is a very large, round metal pot used for cooking over a fire.

words.tr:
adj. 缩成皱纹的；使起波状的
v. （使）起皱褶；“corrugate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The box is made of corrugated cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是由波纹纸板制成的。
words.en: Something that is corrugated has parallel rows of folds that look like a series of waves when viewed from the edge.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.tr: adj. 淫乱的；滥交的；杂乱的
words.ex: He was criticized for his promiscuous behavior.
words.ex_cn: 他因淫乱的行为而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe someone as promiscuous, you disapprove of them because they have sexual relationships with many people. In a more general sense, promiscuous can describe something that is not selective or is mixed without order.

words.tr: adj. 苛求的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is hypercritical about small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对小错误非常吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you say that someone is hypercritical, you mean that they criticize things too much or too severely.

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.tr: n. 滑稽；丑态；插科打诨
words.ex: The play was filled with buffoonery to entertain the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部戏充满了滑稽表演，以娱乐观众。
words.en: Buffoonery refers to behavior that is ridiculous but amusing, often involving silly jokes or actions.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr:
n. 巴洛克式；
adj. 巴洛克式的；
words.ex: The church has a baroque style with gold decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂具有巴洛克风格，装饰有金色元素。
words.en: Baroque is a style of architecture, music, and art that was common in Europe in the 17th and early 18th centuries, characterized by ornate detail.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.tr: n. 优势；支配地位；支配力量
words.ex: The king's ascendancy lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 国王的统治持续了二十年。
words.en: If one group has ascendancy over another group, it has more power or influence than the other group.

words.ex: He gave an absolute yes to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了完全肯定的回答。
words.en: Absolute means complete and total, or not limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.ex: The old house has a vestige of its original design.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子还保留着它原始设计的痕迹。
words.en: A vestige is a small part or amount of something that remains after the rest has disappeared or been destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.ex: The internet created many new neologisms like 'selfie' and 'blog'.
words.ex_cn: 互联网创造了许多新词，比如'selfie'和'blog'。
words.en: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression that may be in the process of entering common use, but has not yet been accepted into mainstream language.

words.ex: She painted with great verve.
words.ex_cn: 她作画时充满热情。
words.en: If you say that someone has verve, you mean that they seem to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr:
adj. 倾心的；被迷住的
v. 迷住；使迷恋；“enamor”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was enamored with the idea of traveling the world.
words.ex_cn: 他迷恋上了环游世界的想法。
words.en: If you are enamored of something or someone, you are very fond of them or very interested in them.

words.tr: v. 谴责；强烈反对；悲叹
words.ex: He deplores the violence on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他谴责电视上的暴力。
words.en: If you deplore something, you think it is very wrong or very bad.

words.ex: The gentry owned most of the land in the old village.
words.ex_cn: 绅士阶层拥有这个古老村庄的大部分土地。
words.en: The gentry are people of high social class, especially in the past.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.tr:
adj. 混乱不清的；引起误解的
v. 混淆；曲解；断章取义；“garble”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The phone call was garbled and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 电话声音杂乱，很难听清楚。
words.en: If something is garbled, it is confused and difficult to understand, often because it has been communicated in a way that is unclear or distorted.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: He enjoyed the adventure through vicarious experiences in books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过书中的间接体验享受了冒险。
words.en: Experienced or felt by watching, hearing about, or reading about someone else rather than by doing something yourself.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe a person, action, or remark as fatuous, you mean that they are extremely silly, showing a lack of intelligence or thought.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；忧愁的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a doleful look after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: A doleful expression, sound, or manner is very sad.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.tr:
n. 旗；旗帜；信号旗；
v. 用旗标记；
words.ex: The flag waves in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: A flag is a piece of cloth with a special design or colors that is used as a symbol, or to give a signal.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.ex: The phoenix rises from its ashes.
words.ex_cn: 凤凰从灰烬中重生。
words.en: A phoenix is a mythical bird that is said to be cyclically regenerated or reborn. Associated with the sun, a phoenix obtains new life by arising from the ashes of its predecessor.

words.ex: He read an elegy for his dead dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为他去世的狗朗读了一首挽歌。
words.en: An elegy is a sad poem, often about someone who has died.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.tr: n. 兵工厂；武器库；军械库；
words.ex: The old arsenal now serves as a museum.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧兵工厂现在被用作博物馆。
words.en: An arsenal is a place where weapons and military equipment are stored or made.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.tr: adj. 不善言辞的；口齿不清的
words.ex: He was inarticulate when he tried to explain the problem.
words.ex_cn: 当他试图解释这个问题时，他表达不清。
words.en: If someone is inarticulate, they are unable to express themselves easily or well in speech.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.tr: adj. 相关的；有联系的； v. 关联；“relate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This book is related to science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书与科学相关。
words.en: If two or more things are related, there is a connection between them.

words.tr: adj. 高雅的； v. “rarefy”的过去式；
words.ex: He enjoys rarefied art and classical music.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢高雅的艺术和古典音乐。
words.en: Rarefied means made less dense or concentrated, especially in the context of air or gases. It can also refer to something that is elevated in character or nature, often in a way that is considered refined or exclusive.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.tr:
n. 讽刺作品
v. 讽刺
words.ex: The cartoon lampooned the president with funny drawings.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画用搞笑的图画讽刺了总统。
words.en: To lampoon someone or something means to criticize them very strongly in a humorous way, especially in a piece of writing.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.tr: adj. 婚姻的；夫妻（关系）的
words.ex: They have a connubial relationship after 30 years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚30年后依然有着婚姻关系。
words.en: Relating to marriage or the relationship between a husband and wife.

words.ex: He loves ichthyology and studies fish every day.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱鱼类学，每天研究鱼类。
words.en: The branch of zoology that deals with the study of fishes.

words.tr: n. 喜怒无常；情绪化；闷闷不乐
words.ex: His moodiness makes it hard to talk to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的情绪化让他很难相处。
words.en: The state of being moody; frequent changes in mood.

words.ex: He made an imprudent decision and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个鲁莽的决定，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as imprudent, you think it is not sensible or carefully thought out.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.ex: Old sailors often got scurvy from lack of fresh fruit.
words.ex_cn: 老水手因缺乏新鲜水果而患上坏血病。
words.en: A disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin C, characterized by spongy and bleeding gums, bleeding under the skin, and extreme weakness.

words.ex: The matriarch runs the family with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 女家长以智慧管理着这个家庭。
words.en: A matriarch is a woman who is the head of a family or tribe.

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.ex: She was aghast when she saw the mess.
words.ex_cn: 她看到那片狼藉时惊呆了。
words.en: If you are aghast, you are filled with horror and surprise.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.tr:
n. 吹牛者；自夸者
adj. 吹牛的
words.ex: He is a braggart who always talks about his wins.
words.ex_cn: 他是个自吹自擂的人，总是谈论自己的胜利。
words.en: A braggart is someone who boasts about their achievements or possessions in a way that is annoying to others.

words.tr: n. 混杂物；集锦；集成曲
words.ex: The band played a medley of old songs.
words.ex_cn: 乐队演奏了一串老歌的混合曲。
words.en: A medley is a mixture of things, especially a mixture of tunes or songs played one after the other.

words.tr: adj. 不能溶解的；不能分解的；不可毁坏的
words.ex: Their friendship was indissoluble, lasting through all the trials and tribulations.
words.ex_cn: 他们的友谊是牢不可破的，经历了所有的考验和磨难。
words.en: If something is indissoluble, it cannot be broken apart or ended.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.ex: The long wait disgruntles the customers.
words.ex_cn: 漫长的等待让顾客感到不满。
words.en: If you are disgruntled, you are angry or dissatisfied because something has not happened the way you wanted.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.ex: He wrote a short epigram about love.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于爱情的短小警句。
words.en: A short poem or sentence that expresses something such as a feeling or idea in a short and clever or funny way.

words.ex: His exceptionable behavior upset the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他令人反感的行为让老师很生气。
words.en: If you describe something as exceptionable, you mean that it is open to objection or criticism.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.ex: The snake slithered through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在草丛中滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and quietly with a twisting or oscillating motion, like a snake.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.ex: He wrote an exegesis of the ancient text.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇对古文的阐释。
words.en: Exegesis is the explanation and interpretation of a text, especially a religious one.

words.ex: He showed conformity with the group's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了小组的规定。
words.en: Conformity is the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or standards.

words.tr:
n. 传教士；牧师；神职人员
adj. 神职者的；牧师的；教会的
words.ex: The ecclesiastic spoke about faith in church.
words.ex_cn: 这位神职人员在教堂里谈论信仰。
words.en: An ecclesiastic is a priest or minister in the Christian Church.

words.ex: The vertex of the triangle is at the top.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的顶点在顶部。
words.en: The highest point of something; the top or apex.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.tr: adj. 极不公正的；邪恶的
words.ex: The judge's iniquitous decision sparked widespread outrage.
words.ex_cn: 法官的不公正判决引发了广泛的愤怒。
words.en: If you describe something as iniquitous, you mean that it is very unfair or morally bad.

words.ex: The fronds of the fern swayed gently in the breeze.
words.ex_cn: 蕨类的叶子在微风中轻轻摇曳。
words.en: A frond is a large, divided leaf, especially of a fern or palm.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.tr: adj. 外界的；外在的；非固有的；
words.ex: The reward was extrinsic, not from within.
words.ex_cn: 这个奖励是外界的，不是来自内心的。
words.en: Extrinsic means not forming part of or belonging to a thing; external.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.ex: I saw a couple of birds flying in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 我看见几只鸟在天上飞。
words.en: A couple is two people who are married, living together, or having a sexual relationship. It can also refer to a small number of things or people.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr:
v. 丢弃；放弃；扔掉
n. 投弃；抛弃；投弃货物
words.ex: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to land safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员不得不抛掉多余的燃料以安全着陆。
words.en: To jettison something means to throw it away or get rid of it, usually because it is not wanted or needed.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.ex: The treaty established amity between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 该条约确立了两国之间的友好关系。
words.en: A friendly relationship between people or countries.

words.ex: He was arrested for bilking investors out of millions of dollars.
words.ex_cn: 他因诈骗投资者数百万美元而被捕。
words.en: To bilk someone means to cheat them, especially out of money.

words.tr:
v. （因发言冗长）妨碍（会议的进程）
n. （议会中为拖延表决的）冗长演说
words.ex: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote on the bill.
words.ex_cn: 参议员使用阻挠议事行动来拖延对该法案的投票。
words.en: A filibuster is a tactic used in a legislative assembly to prevent a measure from being brought to a vote. It is most commonly associated with the U.S. Senate, where a senator or a group of senators may extend debate on a proposal indefinitely to delay or entirely prevent a decision on it.

words.tr: adj. 非常亮的；浓艳的；苍白的；血红的；可怕的；（故意地）骇人听闻的
words.ex: The lurid neon signs lit up the night street.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的霓虹灯照亮了夜晚的街道。
words.en: If you say that something is lurid, you are critical of it because it involves a lot of violence, sex, or shocking detail.

words.ex: He was an ingrate who never thanked anyone for their help.
words.ex_cn: 他是个忘恩负义的人，从不感谢别人的帮助。
words.en: An ingrate is a person who is not grateful for something that has been done for them.

words.ex: He didn't care about an iota of the details.
words.ex_cn: 他对这些细节的极小量都不在意。
words.en: An iota is an extremely small amount of something.

words.ex: The mountains look distant from here.
words.ex_cn: 从这里看，山显得很远。
words.en: If you describe something as distant, you mean that it is far away in space or time.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.tr: adj. 卑屈的；恭顺的；次要的；从属的
words.ex: He is subservient to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板唯命是从。
words.en: If you are subservient, you do whatever someone wants you to do.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.tr: adj. 有怪想的；想入非非的；任性顽固的；脾气坏的
words.ex: He became increasingly crotchety in his old age.
words.ex_cn: 他在老年时变得越来越反复无常。
words.en: If you describe someone as crotchety, you mean they are bad-tempered and easily irritated.

words.ex: He is an atheistic person who doesn't believe in gods.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不相信神的无神论者。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by atheism; denying the existence of God or gods.

words.tr: n. 生活福利设施；便利设施；“amenity”的复数；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等良好的生活福利设施。
words.en: Amenities are things such as stores or sports facilities that are provided for people's convenience, enjoyment, or comfort.

words.tr: v. 狂热地描述；过分赞美；写作狂想诗文
words.ex: She loves to rhapsodize about her travels.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢热情地谈论她的旅行。
words.en: To rhapsodize means to speak or write about someone or something with great enthusiasm and delight.

words.tr:
n. 摘录；摘要
v. 摘录；引用
words.ex: He read an excerpt from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他读了这本书的一段摘录。
words.en: An excerpt is a short piece of writing or music which is taken from a larger piece.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: It was an auspicious day for their wedding.
words.ex_cn: 那天是他们婚礼的吉日。
words.en: If you describe something as auspicious, you mean that it is a sign of future success.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.ex: His cupidity led him to make risky investments.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪导致他进行了高风险的投资。
words.en: Intense desire for wealth or possessions; greed.

words.tr: adj. 革新的；富有革新精神的；
words.ex: The company made an innovative phone.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司推出了一款革新的手机。
words.en: Something that is innovative is new and original, especially in the way that it is done.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.tr: adj. 有浮力的；心情愉快的；
words.ex: The buoyant life jacket keeps you on the water.
words.ex_cn: 有浮力的救生衣让你浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoyant object floats on a liquid or in the air. A buoyant economy, market, or industry is successful because a lot of money is being spent or invested in it.

words.tr: adj. 穿戴土气的；不时髦的
words.ex: She wore a dowdy dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件土气的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or their clothes as dowdy, you mean that their clothes are dull and unfashionable.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.ex: The sun is a bright luminary in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 太阳是天空中一个明亮的发光体。
words.en: A luminary is a person who is very famous and highly respected, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: The injury incapacitated him for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他几周无法行动。
words.en: To make someone unable to do something, especially because of injury or illness.

words.tr:
n. 嘘声；不满之声
v. 发嘘声
words.ex: The audience started catcalling when the speaker made a controversial statement.
words.ex_cn: 当演讲者发表有争议的言论时，观众开始发出嘘声。
words.en: A catcall is a loud whistle or a comment shouted by someone in a crowd, usually expressing disapproval or mockery.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；开玩笑；戏谑
words.ex: He played a prank on his friend with a fake spider.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个假蜘蛛捉弄了他的朋友。
words.en: A prank is a trick or practical joke that is played on someone, often to make them look foolish or to amuse others.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；裂口
adj. 劈开的
v. 劈开；砍开；坚守；信守；忠于；“cleave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The rock has a small cleft where water collects.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石上有一个小裂缝，水会积在那里。
words.en: A cleft is a narrow opening or fissure, especially in a rock or the ground.

words.ex: The city is at a latitude of 40 degrees north.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市位于北纬40度。
words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.tr: adj. 不知疲倦的；不屈不挠的
words.ex: He is an indefatigable worker who never stops.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不知疲倦的工作者，从不停止。
words.en: Someone who is indefatigable can work or continue doing something for a very long time without getting tired.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: The wound began to fester if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果不清洗，伤口就会恶化。
words.en: If a wound festers, it becomes infected, making it worse.

words.ex: She sang a beautiful aria at the opera.
words.ex_cn: 她在歌剧上唱了一段优美的咏叹调。
words.en: An aria is a song for one voice in an opera, often expressing a character's emotions.

words.ex: She sang a beautiful aria at the opera.
words.ex_cn: 她在歌剧上唱了一段优美的咏叹调。
words.en: An aria is a song for one voice in an opera, often expressing a character's emotions.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.ex: He felt stuck in the doldrums after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到陷入低谷。
words.en: The doldrums are a state of inactivity or stagnation, especially in reference to a period of time or a geographical area known for its calm winds.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
